title: Upgrade rustls-webpki patch + gix 0.67 to 0.82+ to clear 20 dependabot alerts
description:
Pre-v0.1.1 release work. Dependabot reports 20 open alerts across two advisories.

HIGH (1 alert): rustls-webpki GHSA-82j2-j2ch-gfr8 — DoS panic on malformed CRL. Patch 0.103.12 → 0.103.13 available, cargo update -p rustls-webpki.

MEDIUM (19 alerts): gix family (18) GHSA-2frx-2596-x5r6 — SHA-1 collision detection missing; gix-date (1) GHSA-6mw6-mj76-grwc — TimeBuf::as_str can return non-UTF-8. Both fixed by bumping gix from 0.67 to 0.82+ in Cargo.toml workspace deps.

Scope: (1) cargo update -p rustls-webpki. (2) bump gix pin in Cargo.toml from 0.67 to 0.82 keeping the same feature set (max-performance-safe, status, revision). (3) fix compile errors in git_branch and workspace segments from API churn across 15 minor versions. (4) re-run full test suite. (5) verify dependabot shows 0 open alerts.

Threat model: linesmith uses gix read-only for branch, ahead/behind, and dirty state. No auth, no sign/verify. SHA-1 collisions at worst mis-name a branch.

Acceptance: dependabot API query for open alerts returns count 0.
close_reason: rustls-webpki patched 0.103.12 → 0.103.13 (clears HIGH GHSA-82j2-j2ch-gfr8). gix bumped 0.67 → 0.82 + explicit sha1 feature (default-features = false had silently stripped sha1, leaving gix-hash::Kind as an empty enum that rustc 1.82+ rejects). API churn handled in data_context/git.rs classify_kind: gix 0.82 consolidated Kind::Bare + Kind::WorkTree{is_linked:false} into Kind::Common and moved bare detection to Repository::is_bare(); Kind::WorkTree{is_linked:true} is now Kind::LinkedWorkTree. Deprecated peel_to_id_in_place replaced with peel_to_id. 950 tests pass, release binary 4.1MB.

title: from_terminal() returns None when stdout is piped; CC spawns always pipe linesmith so TrueColor themes never activate
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 live-capture session. User configured `theme = \"catppuccin-mocha\"` expecting the mocha palette. Under Claude Code (which always spawns with piped stdout), `supports_color::on(Stream::Stdout)` returns None, `from_terminal()` drops to `Capability::None`, and `force_color_detect()` falls back to `Capability::Palette16`. Catppuccin themes then render as default Palette16 ANSI (BrightBlue/BrightBlack/etc.) — indistinguishable from the built-in `default` theme.

Net effect: every TrueColor theme silently downgrades to the 16-color fallback under real CC usage. Mocha/Frappe/Macchiato/Latte all end up identical to `default`.

**Fix sketch:**
- In `Capability::from_terminal()` at `crates/linesmith/src/theme/mod.rs:199`, when `supports_color` returns None, check env independently: `COLORTERM=truecolor|24bit` → TrueColor; `TERM` matching 256color/xterm-ghostty/xterm-kitty/alacritty/tmux-256color → Palette256; else Palette16 (fresh fallback since we know the TTY-capability probe failed but we are still likely being rendered by a real terminal).
- Alternatively: probe stderr as a secondary signal since statusline spawns often leave stderr as a TTY.
- Tests: env fixture with COLORTERM=truecolor and stdout=piped should yield TrueColor; env fixture without COLORTERM should still yield Palette16 (not None), matching current `--force-color` behavior.

**Why this matters:** this is table stakes for a tool that ships curated Catppuccin/Dracula/Nord presets as a v0.1 differentiator (per linesmith-project-vision memory). No user will ever see the catppuccin palette under current detection.
close_reason: force_color_detect rewritten to use Capability::force_from(tty, env) — picks richer of supports-color TTY probe and COLORTERM/TERM env probe, floors at Palette16 so force-color intent is never silently dropped. COLORTERM and TERM threaded through CliEnv snapshot so tests and embedders stay hermetic (Codex P2 regression guard). Auto-color stays pipe-safe: from_terminal unchanged, still returns None when stdout isn't a TTY. Pure helpers from_env_vars and force_from are unit-tested; a hermeticity test locks the CliEnv-only read path.

title: parse_effort rejects Claude Code's object-shaped effort field
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 live-capture. CC 2.1.119 emits:

```json
"effort": {
  "level": "xhigh"
}
```

`parse_effort` at `crates/linesmith/src/input.rs:536-538` expects a bare string:
```rust
let raw = value.as_str().ok_or_else(|| type_mismatch("effort", JsonType::String, JsonType::of(value)))?;
```

This rejects the real payload as TypeMismatch, collapses the whole stdin parse, and renders `?`. Spec at `docs/specs/input-schema.md:358` still says "Claude Code doesnt emit yet" — spec is stale too.

**Fix sketch:**
- Accept the object form `{"level": "xhigh"}` as canonical (thats what CC actually sends).
- Keep bare-string tolerance as a defensive fallback if its ever seen.
- If effort is an object with no `.level`, surface MissingField("effort.level") with full path.
- Update `docs/specs/input-schema.md` edge-case row.
- Tests: object-happy, object-missing-level, bare-string-back-compat, null, absent, type-mismatch (non-object non-string non-null).

**Acceptance:** replaying the captured stdin JSONL record tagged `baseline-200k` through linesmith renders the Opus 4.7 statusline without error, and the effort level flows into `StatusContext.effort = Some(EffortLevel::XHigh)`.

Also surfaced: the pre-existing cargo-installed binary (~/.cargo/bin/linesmith) still has the old stdin `rate_limits` parser that rejects the numeric `resets_at`. Fixed in source (no longer parsed); just needs cargo install --path to refresh.
close_reason: parse_effort accepts both object form {level: string} (canonical per CC 2.1.x live capture) and bare-string (back-compat). Errors carry full JSON path — effort.level for object-form failures, effort for primitive rejection. 8 new tests cover null at outer/inner, missing level, non-string level, unknown values, non-object non-string, and both happy paths. Spec edge-case table updated. Integration fixture claude_worktree.json flipped to object form to exercise the canonical path end-to-end.

title: DataContext::usage() fallback cascade orchestrator
description:
Ties slices 1-5 together. Replaces Arc::new(Err(UsageError::NotImplemented)) in DataContext::usage() with the real cascade per data-fetching.md §OAuth fallback cascade (which reorders ADR-0011 to put cache reads before credentials — same behavior, avoids Keychain subprocess on cache hits).

Cascade order:
1. In-memory OnceCell hit → return
2. Disk cache (usage.json) fresh + schema_version matches → populate memory, return
3. Lock file active AND disk cache has stale data → return stale
4. Read credentials via ctx.credentials() (triggers Keychain subprocess if not yet resolved)
5. No token → record UsageError::Credentials(NoCredentials) → JSONL fallback (step 7)
6. Hit endpoint with 2s timeout → 200 cache+return; 429/timeout/network + stale cache → serve stale; 429/timeout/network without stale → JSONL fallback; 401 → Unauthorized recorded → JSONL fallback
7. JSONL fallback via aggregate_jsonl(): success → return UsageData { source: Jsonl }; failure → surface original recorded error
8. Fresh endpoint 200 writes usage.json AND updates usage.lock with blocked_until = now + cache_duration (other processes see via cache, not retry)

Ships real impl behind DataContext::usage() using slices 1-5; UsageSource::Jsonl tag propagation to segments; UsageApiResponse → UsageData conversion (endpoint path) + JsonlAggregate → UsageData (fallback path).
design: Cache-before-credentials ordering follows data-fetching.md §OAuth fallback cascade explicitly — deliberate departure from ADR-0011 written cascade order for same user-visible behavior. Documented here so future reviewers do not "fix" it back. Lock file write on successful fetch: blocked_until = cached_at + cache_duration. Expired lock = cache stale = other process retries. Error recording order: record first real failure (credentials missing, endpoint error) then try JSONL; on JSONL success error is discarded; on JSONL failure it is surfaced. JsonlError wraps into UsageError::Jsonl(...) per slice 1 taxonomy. No retry loop at this layer; stale-cache serve IS the retry.
acceptance_criteria: Cascade test per branch: fresh-memory, fresh-disk, stale-disk + active-lock, cache-miss + 200, cache-miss + 401, cache-miss + 429 with stale, cache-miss + 429 without stale, cache-miss + timeout with stale, cache-miss + timeout without stale → JSONL success, all-error → original error surfaces. NoCredentials masking guarantee: no token → [No credentials], NOT [Timeout], even when JSONL also fails. Fresh-cache hit does NOT trigger credential resolution (counter on test double). Running linesmith twice with warm usage.json triggers zero HTTP requests and zero Keychain subprocesses. Concurrent processes with stale lock: second process serves stale data. UsageSource flows: endpoint → Endpoint; JSONL → Jsonl (asserted by segment test stub).
close_reason: DataContext::usage() cascade orchestrator: pure resolve_usage function (cache/lock/transport/creds/jsonl/clock injected), wired through DataContext::usage() with defaults. Cache-before-credentials short-circuit; active lock blocks fetch even on cold cache (Codex P1); 429/timeout/401 persist usage.lock with Retry-After or error-TTL backoff so concurrent processes honor it (Codex P1). CredentialError gets lossy Clone so UsageError::Credentials(variant) propagates through Arc-shared boundaries (rate-limit-segments.md error table). write_cache/write_lock debug_assert loudly on failure with TODO(lsm-logger) anchors; reads silently degrade. DataContext::preseed_usage pre-populates the OnceCell so tests and plugin-dev harnesses skip the cascade. v0.1 JSONL path: ctx.usage ignores JSONL result (can't populate tier-aware utilization), follow-up tracked as lsm-xhu.

title: JsonlAggregate + JsonlTailer (5h block + 7d window aggregator)
description:
Terminal fallback source for DataContext::usage(). Scans ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl, aggregates into 5h blocks + 7d windows, dedupes on message.id. Wire shape defined by jsonl-aggregation.md spec (slice 0).

Ships: JsonlAggregate struct + JsonlError taxonomy per jsonl-aggregation.md; JsonlTailer { path, last_offset, last_size } with read_new::<T>() -> Result<Vec<T>, JsonlError> per data-fetching.md §JSONL incremental tail; 5h block aggregation per research/jsonl-data-source.md §3 (port ccusage _session-blocks.ts math); 7d rolling window (second pass); dedup seen message.id within window; project-root discovery cascade $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/ → ~/.config/claude/projects/ → ~/.claude/projects/; truncation/rotation detection (size < last_size → reset offset); aggregate_jsonl() -> Result<JsonlAggregate, JsonlError> entry point consumed by slice 6.
design: Per-process JsonlTailer with last_offset = 0 at start (v0.1 no daemon per ADR-0012). Daemon mode reuse is a spec follow-up. Malformed lines logged at warn!, offset advances past them (per data-fetching.md §JSONL). Tailer does NOT hold file open across calls — opens + reads + closes per invocation; rotation detection via stat before read. Partial struct with #[serde(default)]: only consume documented fields; unknown silently skipped per ADR-0009. Dedup set bounded by 7d window, not whole file — bounded memory regardless of transcript size.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: empty file, single line, many lines, truncation, partial trailing line (no \\n), malformed JSON lines logged + skipped, offset monotonicity invariant. 5h block boundary tests: entries exactly 5h apart, entries within 5h, gap-block emission for idle >5h. Dedup tests: same message.id twice → counted once. Directory-cascade tests: only $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/ exists → read from there; none exist → JsonlError::DirectoryMissing. Integration test: realistic multi-file fixture under tests/fixtures/jsonl/ matching actual Claude Code output; aggregate output matches ccusage reference.
close_reason: JSONL aggregator: offset-tailing JsonlTailer, project-root cascade ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR → XDG → ~/.claude) with dedicated XDG-without-HOME handling, ccusage-derived 5h billing-block math with FiveHourBlock::end method, 7d window with clock-skew guard. Non-UTF-8 lines skip per-line via read_until + lossy convert (not whole-file abort). 30+ tests cover boundary math, cross-root dedup, offset monotonicity, and clock-skew edge cases.

title: OAuth /api/oauth/usage HTTP client (ureq + retry/timeout/backoff)
description:
HTTP surface between the fallback orchestrator (slice 6) and the Anthropic OAuth usage endpoint. Returns Result<UsageApiResponse, UsageError>; orchestrator layers cache + credentials + JSONL fallback on top.

Ships: fetch_usage(creds: &Credentials, timeout: Duration) -> Result<UsageApiResponse, UsageError>. Headers per ADR-0011 §Endpoint contract: Authorization: Bearer {token}, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, User-Agent: linesmith/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}. 2s default timeout. Status handling: 200 → deserialize; 401 → Unauthorized; 429 → parse Retry-After (integer-seconds AND HTTP-date per ADR-0011) → RateLimited { retry_after }; 4xx/5xx other → NetworkError; timeout/connect failure → Timeout/NetworkError; malformed JSON → ParseError.
design: ureq (project-standard). No async runtime. Inject HTTP surface via small trait (UsageEndpoint) with blanket impl over ureq::Agent so tests swap a fake — avoids mockito dev-dep balloon. Retry-After HTTP-date parser: httpdate crate. Token redaction: format!("Bearer {}", creds.token()) locally, never logged; if ureq adds trace-level request logging later we add a redaction hook. No retry loop — this is the bottom layer; retries (stale-cache serve, JSONL fallback) live in slice 6.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests with trait-injected HTTP surface (or mockito) covering: 200 happy path; 401; 429 with integer Retry-After; 429 with HTTP-date Retry-After; 429 without Retry-After (default 300s backoff); timeout; connect refused; malformed JSON. Golden-fixture integration: feed live-captured response, assert deserialization matches. Token does not appear in any error Display/Debug output when request fails with 401 (verified via format!). User-Agent string includes CARGO_PKG_VERSION.
close_reason: OAuth /api/oauth/usage HTTP client landed in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/fetcher.rs (~500 LOC + 23 tests). UsageTransport trait + UreqTransport impl + fetch_usage(); maps HTTP statuses onto UsageError taxonomy per rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table. Retry-After parsed as integer or RFC 9110 HTTP-date with 24h cap + 300s fallback. Response body capped at 64 KiB. User-Agent cached on struct + exposed via default_user_agent() for regression testing. Workspace MSRV raised to 1.85 for ureq 3.3 + rustls. Credentials::for_testing helper added. 623 tests passing. Unblocks lsm-wwd (cascade orchestrator).

title: Multi-tier OAuth usage cache (usage.json + usage.lock + atomic rename)
description:
Disk-backed layer of the cache stack per data-fetching.md §OAuth usage cache stack + §Atomic writes + §Concurrent processes. In-memory OnceCell already on DataContext; this slice adds disk tiers and lock file.

Ships: CacheStore with read() -> Result<Option<CachedUsage>, CacheError> + write(&CachedUsage); CachedUsage { schema_version: u32, cached_at: DateTime<Utc>, data: Option<UsageApiResponse>, error: Option<CachedError> } matching data-fetching.md shape; LockStore with read() + write(blocked_until: u64, error: &str); atomic-rename writes via tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist; schema_version mismatch → treat as miss; path resolution XDG_CACHE_HOME/linesmith/ → ~/.cache/linesmith/; default 180s data TTL (configurable via usage.cache_duration), 30s error TTL, 30s lock TTL.
design: One module (cache.rs) owning both CacheStore + LockStore; shared path-resolution and atomic-write helpers. schema_version = 1 for v0.1, const so bumps visible in review. CachedError mirrors UsageError taxonomy but serialized as tagged string ("NoCredentials", "Timeout", etc.) — NOT the full Rust enum with inner CredentialError data. Errors cached briefly (30s) are intentionally lossy across process boundaries — live errors from this process take precedence. Directory creation via fs::create_dir_all at write time, not init. Lock file coordination uses SAME atomic-rename helper as data writes; no flock/LockFileEx gymnastics.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip: write → read returns equivalent CachedUsage. schema_version mismatch → read() returns Ok(None) (miss, not error). Clock skew (cached_at > now) → treated as stale miss. Zero-byte/corrupt cache file → Ok(None) miss, never hard-errors. Concurrent write smoke: 2 threads both writing different payloads; assert final file is one-or-the-other, never interleaved (atomic rename demo). Lock file round-trip including legacy non-JSON fallback (mtime+30s implicit blocked_until per data-fetching.md §Lock file shape).
close_reason: Disk cache + lock file landed in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/cache.rs (~830 LOC + 20 tests). CacheStore + LockStore + atomic_write_json (tempfile::persist). CachedData nests unknown_buckets as named field (vs wire-flatten). Lock.blocked_until capped at now + 24h against pathological values. Non-UTF-8 / malformed → Ok(None) or legacy-mtime fallback per spec. Percent + UsageBucket + ExtraUsage + UsageApiResponse gain Serialize for cache roundtrip. tempfile moved dev-deps → runtime. 646 tests passing. Unblocks lsm-wwd (cascade orchestrator). Follow-ups: lsm-038 (structured diagnostics when logger lands), lsm-752 (Lock schema_version for future-compat).

title: Credential reader: Keychain primary + multi-account fallback + file cascade
description:
Per credentials.md §Interface + §Resolution cascade. Replaces CredentialError::NotImplemented stub in data_context::credentials().

Ships: Credentials { token: SecretString, scopes: Vec<String>, source: CredentialSource } with Debug redacting the token; CredentialSource (5 variants: MacosKeychainPrimary, MacosKeychainMultiAccount {service, mdat}, EnvDir, XdgConfig, ClaudeLegacy); CredentialError (6 variants: NoCredentials, SubprocessFailed, IoError, ParseError, MissingField, EmptyToken); resolve_credentials() entry point; #[cfg(target_os="macos")] primary via `security find-generic-password -a $USER -w -s "Claude Code-credentials"` + multi-account fallback via `security dump-keychain` with mdat sort + per-candidate find-generic-password retry; all platforms file cascade $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json → ~/.config/claude/.credentials.json → ~/.claude/.credentials.json with 1MB size cap; wire into DataContext::credentials() with process-lifetime memoization.
design: secrecy crate for SecretString (already referenced in credentials.md). `security` invoked via std::process::Command with Stdin::null() and a short deadline matching endpoint budget. mdat parsing: hex-ASCII blobs from `security dump-keychain`; stable sort, mdat-DESC (newest first), no-mdat entries last by dump order. File size cap: 1MB hard limit pre-parse → ParseError if exceeded. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="" → treated as unset (user-intent honoring). No Windows Credential Manager (v0.2+ per ADR-0011).
acceptance_criteria: resolve_credentials unit tests per credentials.md §Testing strategy (valid JSON, null token, missing field, invalid JSON, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to existing/non-existing, XDG preferred over legacy, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="" treated as unset). #[cfg(target_os="macos")] integration: inject fake `security` binary on PATH returning controlled output; assert primary path, multi-account fallback, mdat sort picks newest. Credentials::Debug does NOT leak token (visual assert with format!). Token never at trace/debug level (grep tests/ for bare token use). DataContext::credentials() returns cached Arc<Result<...>>; subprocess invoked once per process.
close_reason: Credential reader + OAuth token resolution landed in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/credentials.rs (~850 LOC + 30 tests). Credentials/CredentialSource/CredentialError types with SecretString-redacted Debug; flat code() taxonomy; resolve_credentials() runs the cascade (macOS Keychain primary + multi-account mdat-newest + file cascade). macOS run_security enforces 2s + 500ms grace via try_wait polling with reader-thread drain; errSecItemNotFound (44) falls through cleanly; other non-zero exits preserve stderr (truncated at 512 bytes). AccessToken uses Option<Option<String>> with deserialize_with to distinguish MissingField from EmptyToken. FileCascadeEnv DI sidesteps unsafe env mutation. DataContext::credentials() wired + memoized. 602 tests passing. Unblocks lsm-7xv (HTTP), lsm-wwd (cascade), lsm-l35 (doctor). Follow-ups filed: lsm-yq8 (macOS PATH-injection integration test), lsm-iz6 (plugin-api.md MissingField/EmptyToken taxonomy update).

title: UsageApiResponse (wire) + UsageData/UsageSource/UsageError (internal) types
description:
Foundation types for every other y6m slice. Replaces the #[non_exhaustive] pub struct UsageData {} stub + single-variant UsageError::NotImplemented in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/mod.rs and errors.rs.

Ships: UsageApiResponse (wire shape per ADR-0011 §Endpoint contract) with Option<UsageBucket> fields (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_oauth_apps), Option<ExtraUsage>, #[serde(flatten)] unknown_buckets: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value> catch-all. UsageBucket { utilization: Percent, resets_at: DateTime<Utc> } reusing input::Percent (already has [0,100] clamp). ExtraUsage per rate-limit-segments.md §extra_usage. UsageData (internal) = wire fields + source: UsageSource { Endpoint, Jsonl } tag used by stale_marker rendering. UsageError (flat, 8 variants) per rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table: NoCredentials, Credentials(CredentialError), Timeout, RateLimited { retry_after: Option<Duration> }, NetworkError, ParseError, Unauthorized, Jsonl(JsonlError).
design: Wire shape (UsageApiResponse) separate from internal (UsageData) so endpoint-client → cache → segment conversion is explicit — slice 3 owns UsageApiResponse → UsageData (endpoint path), slice 5 owns JsonlAggregate → UsageData (fallback path). UsageError::Credentials(CredentialError) wrapping (docs-review Decision 1) over flat 8 variants: segment renderer matches on inner variant for three credential-flavored strings [Keychain error]/[Credentials unreadable]/[No credentials]. Percent reuse: input::Percent::new(f32) → Option<Self>; no new type. #[serde(default)] on every Option field so partial responses never fail parse. #[non_exhaustive] on UsageApiResponse and UsageError for non-breaking growth.
acceptance_criteria: Golden-fixture serde round-trip: feed live-captured /api/oauth/usage response from docs/research/claude-data-files.md §Raw data, assert lossless parse; feed a response with an injected codename ("quokka_experimental") and assert it lands in unknown_buckets. Error rendering smoke test: for each UsageError variant, produce the exact rendered string per rate-limit-segments.md table. UsageData exposes source(), five_hour(), seven_day(), extra_usage() accessors. ctx.usage() still returns an Err sentinel until slice 6 wires the real fetcher.

title: Catppuccin Role::Muted remapped from overlay0 to subtext0 (live-capture readability fix)
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 live-capture session on 2026-04-24. `Role::Muted` previously mapped to `overlay0` (Catppuccin UI-chrome grey meant for borders/dividers). Cost and effort segments render with `Muted`, so on Catppuccin dark flavors (Mocha at `#6c7086`) they sat too dim to read on dark terminal backgrounds.

**Rationale:** `overlay0` is the correct role for `Border`, not for text. Catppuccin semantics: `text` > `subtext1` > `subtext0` for text; `overlay2/1/0` and `surface2/1/0` for UI chrome. Our `Border` role already maps to `surface2`, so users who wanted the chrome-grey have it via that role.

**Test coverage:** existing palette-drift tests pass; no new test needed for a color mapping (the `every_flavor_maps_every_base_role` test guards against unmapping).

**Acceptance:** live statusline under Claude Code shows `$21.12` and `xhigh` in a clearly readable grey (`#a6adc8`) instead of the near-invisible `#6c7086`.

This issue exists mainly to give the commit for the remap a bead to close per AGENTS.md's "close before staging" convention.

title: Extend ContextWindow to parse current_usage from stdin (prereq for tokens segments)
description:
Prerequisite for lsm-ua8 (tokens segments) and lsm-inpf/lsm-r1w follow-ups that need per-turn token counts.

Currently `crates/linesmith/src/input.rs` captures only `used`, `size`, `total_input_tokens`, `total_output_tokens` on `ContextWindow`. Claude Code's stdin also carries:

```json
"context_window": {
    ...
    "current_usage": {
      "input_tokens": 2000,
      "output_tokens": 500,
      "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
      "cache_read_input_tokens": 500
    }
}
```

This is `null` before the first API call in a session and present afterward.

**Scope:**
- Add `pub struct CurrentUsage` with the four `u64` fields.
- Extend `ContextWindow` with `pub current_usage: Option<CurrentUsage>`.
- Update `parse_context_window` to parse the object when present, map `null` to `None`, and return a `TypeMismatch` when the value is a non-object / non-null.
- Mirror `current_usage` to plugins via `ctx_mirror.rs` as `ctx.status.context_window.current_usage` — either a map with the four keys or rhai `()` when None.
- Update `docs/specs/plugin-api.md` §ctx.status.context_window shape to document the field.
- Tests: present-case parse, null-case parse, missing-case parse (current_usage key absent — treat same as null), type-mismatch error, plugin mirror for both None and Some.

**Acceptance:** parsing + mirror + spec match the stdin contract documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline. `cargo test -p linesmith` green after extending the input fixture suites.

**Blocks:** lsm-ua8 (tokens segments depend on this struct shape). Also unblocks future `context_usable` segment work per lsm-4wb research.

ContextWindow gains Option<TurnUsage> current_usage; parse_current_usage handles absent/null → None and surfaces full nested paths on TypeMismatch/MissingField. ctx_mirror.rs emits ctx.status.context_window.current_usage as map-or-unit via build_turn_usage (destructured to fail compile on new fields). docs/specs/plugin-api.md updated to document the 4 leaf fields — previous one-line reference was aspirational; spec drift closed. 6 unit tests + 1 plugin-mirror test (absent, null, happy-path, non-object TypeMismatch, nested-path TypeMismatch provenance, missing-inner MissingField). title: Widen Percent::from_f64 to clamp used_percentage instead of rejecting >100
description:
Per lsm-4wb research: `Percent::from_f64` at `crates/linesmith/src/input.rs:~555` rejects any value outside `0.0..=100.0` as `ParseError::InvalidValue`. For `context_window.used_percentage` specifically, this collapses the whole stdin parse and degrades the statusline to `?` (driver.rs:719-730).

Claude Code has been observed emitting values >100 post-`/compact` (Anthropic #37163). When that happens linesmith goes marker-state instead of showing a percentage. ccstatusline handles the same case via `clampPercentage(0, 100)` — a bounded display of 100% is better UX than a bare `?` marker.

**Fix sketch:**
- Either widen the `Percent::from_f64` range (accept 0..=200 and let callers clamp) or — cleaner — add a `Percent::from_f64_clamped` constructor and use it in `parse_context_window`. Emit an `lsm_warn!` on clamp so the signal is still visible to users debugging weird percentages.
- Preserve the strict constructor for other callers (`UsageBucket.utilization`, `ContextWindow.used` in rate-limit buckets where 0..=100 is a real contract).
- Test: seed a stdin payload with `used_percentage: 101.3`, assert the segment renders 100% with a warn, not `?`.

**v0.1 significance:** fixes a severe-but-narrow failure mode observed upstream. The defensive parse is cheap and independent of the live-test investigation tracked separately.
close_reason: Percent::from_f64_clamped added; parse_context_window asymmetric: clamp above 100 (known upstream drift per claude-code#37163) with lsm_warn, reject below 0 (undocumented state, preserves corrupted-payload signal). 5 tests (1 unit + 4 integration) cover happy path, fractional overshoot, NaN, and negative-reject. Codex called out the symmetry regression during review; asymmetric design lands the fix without silently masking corrupted inputs. Follow-ups filed: lsm-g3im (tolerance filter on the warn, needs live-test data to calibrate), lsm-inpf ((Percent, Clamp) enum return for compile-time clamp awareness).

title: plugins: cap unknown_buckets size and JSON depth in ctx_mirror
description:
ctx_mirror::build_unknown_buckets iterates a server-controlled HashMap with no size cap. rhai's MAX_MAP_SIZE (256) only gates script-side growth; it does not reject a host-constructed Map with >256 entries. A malicious or buggy /api/oauth/usage response with thousands of keys flows straight through.

Related: json_to_dynamic recurses into arbitrary-depth nested JSON with no depth guard. rhai's MAX_EXPR_DEPTH gates script parsing, not host-side recursion — a nested-object bomb could blow the stack.

Fix: enforce MAX_MAP_SIZE + a key-length cap at the mirror boundary with a lsm_warn! on overshoot. Add a depth limit to json_to_dynamic (recursion counter param or iteration limit).

Found in lsm-xhu silent-failure review #5.
notes: Shipped: CapPosture {Strict, EscapeHatch} split — ctx.status.raw preserves escape-hatch round-trip (depth cap only for stack safety); server-controlled payloads (unknown_buckets values) get full caps (depth, map/array breadth, string size, key size). ConversionLimits aggregates per-category counts into one lsm_warn per top-level call. Deterministic sort on unknown_buckets truncation. docs/specs/plugin-api.md updated. 17 boundary/behavior tests covering exact boundaries, UTF-8 char-boundary truncation, per-entry depth reset, and posture asymmetry. Follow-ups: lsm-p5sx (ctx.meta.truncated sentinel, ADR-sized), lsm-860n (logger test sink).
close_reason: ctx_mirror: cap unknown_buckets at MAX_MAP_SIZE, drop oversize keys (>MAX_STRING_SIZE), and bound json_to_dynamic recursion at MAX_JSON_DEPTH=32 with lsm_warn on overshoot. 3 tests added.

title: rate-limit: 401 + active-lock serves stale endpoint data (pre-existing)
description:
Sequence: invocation A writes a failure lock on 401 (no cache update, intentional per the spec). Invocation B within the 30s error TTL sees the active lock and stale cache, enters the lock-active branch, and serves the stale endpoint data — violating the '401 does not serve stale' policy via the lock-active path.

Pre-existing bug surfaced during lsm-xhu review (silent-failure-hunter #A). Covered only for invocation A by endpoint_401_does_not_serve_stale_cache; no test covers the A→B sequence.

Fix sketch: in the lock-active branch, check entry.error == Some('Unauthorized') and fall through to JSONL (now that JSONL is wired) instead of serving stale data.
close_reason: lock-active branch now skips entry.data when lock.error == Unauthorized, closing the A→B stale-serve path. 3 tests added (A→B with empty JSONL, A→B with JSONL fallback, isolated guard). 401 handler intentionally keeps cache untouched — caching the Unauthorized tag would outlive the 30s lock TTL and mask a subsequent unrelated lock (Codex-flagged state leak).

title: Structured logger + doctor integration for silent Ok(None) paths
description:
Rate-limit segments (lsm-7po) and the usage cascade (lsm-wwd) have multiple `Ok(None)` hide paths and `let _ = write(...)` persistence drops that are currently invisible to users debugging 'why does my statusline look wrong?'.

Scope:
- Wire a `tracing`/`log`-style facade crate-wide with a `RUST_LOG`-ish env gate
- At every rate-limit `Ok(None)` site (bucket absent, resets_at missing, resets_at past, is_enabled=false, format_extra_usage returns None): emit a `debug!` with the gating condition
- At every cascade `write_cache`/`write_lock` failure site (currently `debug_assert!` + TODO(lsm-logger)): promote to a structured `warn!` that `linesmith doctor` can surface
- Wire `linesmith doctor` to read buffered traces and reformat into actionable remediation output
- Drop every `TODO(lsm-logger)` anchor comment in cascade.rs once landed

Blast radius: cascade.rs (6 anchor sites), 5 rate-limit segments (~8 Ok(None) paths total).

Cache/lock read errors escalate PermissionDenied/ENOSPC/corrupt-parse to warn via io::ErrorKind match; NotFound/UnexpectedEof stay debug. Write-side lsm_warn! fires before debug_assert! so release builds still surface data loss. Doctor integration deferred to lsm-l35 (not yet open). Hide-reason channel design gap filed as lsm-45gx.

title: JSONL → UsageBucket mapping for rate-limit segments
description:

2. Distinct `UsageData::Jsonl { tokens: JsonlTokens }` variant (biggest design change; type-design-analyzer's preferred approach)

title: linesmith doctor: usage/credentials/cache diagnostics
description:
Per doctor.md spec (peek before implementation). Reports actionable diagnostics for the y6m data pipeline so users can self-serve before filing issues.

title: Update plugin-api.md to describe rhai plugin data_deps declaration
description:

title: Research: JSON parser + cache serialization stack due-diligence
description:
Before writing Rust code for the data-fetching layer (lsm-y6m + supporting beads), survey the actual parser/serialization landscape with real benchmarks. Outputs decision matrix per source.

Context: docs/research/data-fetching-strategy.md §Parsing efficiency claims serde_json + partial structs is fastest pragmatic choice. Need due-diligence to either validate or refute that claim with real numbers, not estimates.

Acceptance:
- Survey current Rust JSON parsers: serde_json, simd-json, sonic-rs, json-rust, plus anything else relevant
- Real benchmark numbers for our workloads: small <10KB (settings.json, sessions/*.json, OAuth response), medium ~125KB (~/.claude.json), JSONL streaming (MB+)
- Crate maturity signals: last commit, downloads/month, open issues, MSRV, transitive dep count + binary size impact
- What comparable Rust CLIs use for hot-path JSON: ripgrep, fd, bat, gitui, jujutsu, eza, dust, hyperfine — pull their Cargo.tomls
- Memory mapping (memmap2 vs read-into-Vec): edge cases, JSONL append-during-read, Windows quirks
- Internal cache serialization options: bincode vs rkyv vs postcard vs JSON. Decode speed, schema-migration story, inspectability
- JSONL-specialized libraries (jsonl crate, etc.) — anything purpose-built we're missing
- Decision matrix: per data source, recommended parser + format with explicit tradeoff
- Output: docs/research/json-parsing-stack.md (then promote relevant decisions to an ADR slice)

Why now: This is the last research gap before implementation begins on the data-fetching layer. Locking in parser choices speculatively (rather than measuring) creates churn later.
notes: Promoted from a conversation about whether serde_json is fast enough. User flagged: 'I just want to make sure we do our due diligence before starting it.'
close_reason: serde_json + partial structs is the validated v0.1 choice. 9 of 13 surveyed Rust CLIs use serde_json on hot paths; zero use simd-json or sonic-rs. Partial-struct deserialization drops ~/.claude.json parse cost 80%+ — bigger win than swapping parsers. Cache stays JSON (pretty + schema_version) for inspectability; binary saves negligible time at 1KB. JSONL incremental tail via BufReader::read_line + byte offset; mmap contraindicated due to SIGBUS-on-rotation. simd-json deferred behind --features fast-json flag, promotion only on benchmarked >2ms p50 win. bincode upstream archived 2025-08-15 — flagged for future binary-cache decisions. Full doc: docs/research/json-parsing-stack.md.

- Powerline emission: the chevron between two adjacent segments gets Role::Surface for bg, next segment's role for fg. Layout needs theme access (already has it via render_with_warn).
- Tests: snapshot powerline output between two styled segments under Palette16 and None capabilities.

Motivation: completes the `[layout_options]` contract. Part of the v0.1 theming experience.

title: RFC: Extract CLI driver + segment builder from lib.rs
description:
## Problem

lib.rs is ~1300 lines and co-hosts five concerns: the render façade (`run`, `run_with_width`, `run_with_segments_and_width`, `run_with_context`, `RenderContext`), width detection, segment assembly with override validation, the CLI driver (`CliEnv`, `cli_main`, `run_cli`, `load_config`, `check_config`, `resolve_theme`), and ~740 lines of tests across two inline modules. Navigating any single concern requires understanding the whole file; adding tests to one domain requires reading the others. The render façade legitimately belongs at the crate root, but the CLI orchestration and segment assembly are implementation details that leak into the public-API file.

## Proposed Interface

Two new modules, each with a minimal surface. All existing `linesmith::*` paths preserved via re-exports; `main.rs` and `tests/integration.rs` do not change.

### `crate::driver` (new file `src/driver.rs`)

Public surface — two items:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct CliEnv {
    pub linesmith_config: Option<String>,
    pub xdg_config_home: Option<String>,
    pub home: Option<String>,
    pub terminal_width: Option<u16>,
    pub color_capability: Option<crate::theme::Capability>,
}

impl CliEnv {
    pub fn from_process() -> Self;  // snapshot real env
    pub fn for_tests() -> Self;     // None paths, width=Some(200), capability=Some(None)
    pub fn empty() -> Self;         // all None — for tests asserting on lazy detection
}

pub fn cli_main<A>(
    args: A,
    stdin: impl std::io::Read,
    stdout: &mut dyn std::io::Write,
    stderr: &mut dyn std::io::Write,
    env: &CliEnv,
) -> u8
where A: IntoIterator, A::Item: Into<std::ffi::OsString>;
```

Crate-private: `run_cli`, `load_config`, `check_config`, `resolve_theme` become `fn` (no `pub`).

### `crate::segments::builder` (new file `src/segments/builder.rs`)

Public surface — two items:

```rust
pub fn build(config: Option<&crate::config::Config>, warn: impl FnMut(&str)) -> Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>;
pub fn build_default() -> Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>;
```

Crate-private: `apply_override`.

### Crate-root re-exports (in `lib.rs`)

```rust
pub use driver::{cli_main, CliEnv};
pub use segments::builder::{build as build_segments, build_default as build_default_segments};
```

Rename-on-re-export preserves integration-test call sites.

## Dependency Strategy

**In-process** — all logic is pure plus thin I/O wrappers. Nothing crosses a network/process boundary. No new traits or adapters introduced; external-crate wrappers (`supports-color`, `terminal-size`, `toml`, `serde_json`) already live as single-function seams that can be swapped in place.

## Testing Strategy

**Test relocation** — replace, don't layer:

- `cli_main_tests` module (15 tests, ~540 lines) moves from `lib.rs` → `driver.rs`
- `build_segments_*` tests (~8 tests, plus `StubWithWidth` + `width_merge_*` = 12 tests total, ~200 lines) move from `lib.rs::tests` → `segments/builder.rs::tests`
- Width detection tests + `resolve_terminal_width` tests stay in `lib.rs`
- Render-path tests (`malformed_json_renders_marker_and_succeeds`, `minimal_payload_renders_model_then_workspace`, `full_payload_renders_model_context_workspace`) stay in `lib.rs`
- Integration tests at `tests/integration.rs` untouched

**No new tests added** — this is a move refactor. Test count stays at 240 lib + 7 integration.

**New `CliEnv::for_tests()` constructor** replaces the duplicated `fn empty_env()` helper inside `cli_main_tests`. Net LOC reduction ~10 lines of test setup.

## Implementation Recommendations

### What `driver` owns

- Args → exit code (the full CLI lifecycle)
- Config path resolution, load, validation
- `--check-config` exit-code contract (0 ok / 1 invalid)
- Lazy width + capability detection on render path only
- Theme name resolution with unknown-name warning + fallback
- IO wiring through injected stdin/stdout/stderr sinks

### What `driver` hides

- That arg parsing goes through `lexopt` via `cli::parse`
- That config loading is a two-step resolve-then-read
- That `--check-config` has four failure modes (no-path / invalid-parse / no-file-implicit / valid-with-warnings)
- The specific env vars (`LINESMITH_CONFIG`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HOME`) and their precedence

### What `driver` exposes

- `CliEnv` as the sole input struct for ambient process state
- `cli_main` as the sole orchestration entry point
- `u8` exit code (callers wrap in `ExitCode` at the binary boundary)

### What `segments::builder` owns

- `Config` → `Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>` transformation
- Validation: unknown IDs warn + skip, duplicates keep-first, empty-list warning, inverted-bounds drop with warning
- Override application: priority + width-with-inherit-from-inner-default

### What `segments::builder` hides

- The `DEFAULT_SEGMENT_IDS` canonical order
- The `OverriddenSegment` wrapper (applied internally when a `[segments.<id>]` table exists)
- Width-bounds merge algorithm (caller supplies half-specified bounds; builder inherits the other half from the segment's built-in default)

### What `segments::builder` exposes

- Two free functions keyed on `Option<&Config>` + warn callback
- Return type `Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>` unchanged from today

### Migration

- `main.rs` and `tests/integration.rs` keep working unchanged — re-exports handle the path shift
- `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `lib.rs` loses its width + build_segments blocks but keeps render tests
- No public API deletions; no breaking changes

## Scope boundary

Explicitly NOT in this refactor:
- Extension traits for plugin runtime (`lsm-ewa` owns that design)
- Theme registry trait for user-loaded themes (`lsm-qp5` owns that)
- External-crate leak tightening (separate bead — tighten `lexopt::Error` / `toml::de::Error` surfaces out of public API)
- `cli_main_from_process()` convenience wrapper (net-zero move, adds surface for no gain)
- `theme::catppuccin` sketch (belongs in `lsm-b7u`)

## Expected impact

- `lib.rs`: ~1300 → ~400 lines (render façade + width + re-exports + render tests)
- `driver.rs`: new, ~250 lines + ~540 test lines
- `segments/builder.rs`: new, ~90 lines + ~210 test lines
- Public API: zero surface change
- Test count: unchanged (240 lib + 7 integration)
- Follow-ups enabled: any future module deepening can happen inside `driver` or `builder` without touching `lib.rs`
close_reason: Extracted CLI driver into crate::driver and segment assembly into crate::segments::builder. lib.rs: 1206 → 273 lines (77% reduction). Both new modules pub(crate) so re-exports at crate root (linesmith::cli_main, linesmith::CliEnv, linesmith::build_segments, linesmith::build_default_segments) are the canonical paths. Added CliEnv::for_tests() named constructor replacing the anonymous empty_env() helper. Test count unchanged (240 lib + 7 integration). No public API change. Codex review + 5-agent review pass confirmed byte-identical behavior.

title: Slice 7c: User theme TOML loading + themes list subcommand
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn. Lets users drop a theme file into `~/.config/linesmith/themes/` and reference it from config.

**Scope:**
- Theme TOML file format parser (per docs/specs/theming.md §Theme file format): required `name`, `[roles]` base table, optional `[roles.extended]` table, optional `[separators]` table (for lsm-1my forward-compat)
- Color parsing in theme files: hex (`"#rgb"`, `"#rrggbb"`), named 16-color (`"red"`), RGB (`"rgb(r, g, b)"`) — normalized to `Color::TrueColor` or `Color::Palette16`
- User theme discovery: walk `~/.config/linesmith/themes/*.toml` at startup, XDG-compliant
- Name-collision handling: user theme wins over built-in of same name; stderr warning
- Parse error handling: one rejected theme doesn't abort startup; warn with file path + row/col, fall back to `default` if the config asks for the rejected theme
- `linesmith themes list` CLI subcommand: enumerate built-ins + user themes with source annotation (`built-in` vs `~/.config/linesmith/themes/mocha.toml`)

**Out of scope (separate bead):**
- Style string syntax (`"role:success bold"`, `"fg:#ff8800 underline"`) — orthogonal to theme files
- Per-segment style overrides via `[segments.<id>] style = "..."` in config.toml
- Catppuccin conformance tests against user-authored theme files (ships with lsm-b7u already)

**Acceptance:** drop a `mytheme.toml` in `~/.config/linesmith/themes/`, reference it via `theme = "mytheme"` in config.toml, see it render. `linesmith themes list` shows both built-in and user themes with source paths. Name collision with a built-in shows a warning and the user theme wins.
close_reason: User theme TOML loading + themes list subcommand. Users drop files in ~/.config/linesmith/themes/*.toml (XDG-aware); merged into a ThemeRegistry alongside built-ins. Color parsing supports hex (#rgb / #rrggbb), named 16-color, rgb(r,g,b), and 'none'. Two-phase parse with validate_theme_file_keys catches typos at top-level, [roles], [roles.extended], and [separators] with file-path-prefixed warnings. First-user-found wins on collision per spec §Edge cases; user always wins over built-in. New cli::Action::ThemesList subcommand prints registered themes with source annotation. 329 lib + 7 integration tests (up from 290).

title: Slice 7b: Catppuccin flavors (Latte/Frappé/Macchiato/Mocha)
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (MVP theme engine). Ships the 4 Catppuccin flavors against the MVP theme registry so linesmith qualifies for the Catppuccin integration list (github.com/catppuccin/catppuccin#portlist).

Scope:
- Depend on `catppuccin` crate (~20KB) OR embed 4 TOML palettes via include_str!. Decision point during implementation; crate is leaner for palette drift detection.
- Register 4 flavors in the built-in theme registry: catppuccin-latte, catppuccin-frappe, catppuccin-macchiato, catppuccin-mocha
- Map all 9 base roles to Catppuccin palette colors per flavor
- Map all 7 extended roles to flavor-appropriate dim/surface/border variants
- Snapshot tests: render a canonical status-line through each flavor, assert expected bytes
- Palette-sync CI check: detect upstream Catppuccin palette changes

Acceptance: `theme = "catppuccin-mocha"` in config.toml renders with the Mocha palette; 4 flavors all recognized; snapshot tests lock the output per flavor.
close_reason: Catppuccin flavors (Latte/Frappé/Macchiato/Mocha) shipped against the lsm-7kn theme engine. Palette values sourced from the catppuccin crate (v2) so upstream drift is caught by dep bumps. Role mapping follows ecosystem convention: mauve=Primary, blue=Accent, green/yellow/red/teal=state roles, surface0/surface2 for Surface/Border. Dim variants left unset for Catppuccin's single-shade-per-hue identity. 9 new tests including per-flavor mauve drift alarm with canonical RGB values. 290 lib + 7 integration.

title: Make main.rs run() and check_config() testable via pure inner fn
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) review: main.rs has ~100 lines of orchestration (arg error paths, load/fallback logic, --check-config branches) with zero direct tests. Integration tests hit linesmith::run_* which bypasses main entirely.

Extract pure inner function: fn run_inner(args, stdin, stdout, stderr, env) -> ExitCode. Then main.rs becomes a thin wrapper that reads env + delegates. Tests spawn the inner function with fake IO and assert exit codes + byte output.

Alternative: use assert_cmd / std::process::Command to spawn the built binary against fixture configs. Simpler but slower and less portable.

Closing the gap matters because --check-config's exit codes (0 for ok, 1 for invalid) are the CI/editor-integration contract per docs/specs/config.md:245. Today a regression that flips those codes ships green.
notes: Expanded scope post-Codex review: also threaded stderr through run_with_segments_and_width + layout::render (superseded lsm-v3e), and changed terminal_width to Option<u16> so meta commands don't probe TTY.
close_reason: Extracted cli_main(args, stdin, stdout, stderr, env) -> u8 into lib.rs; main.rs shrinks to a 10-line ExitCode wrapper. 12 new tests lock --check-config exit codes (0 ok / 1 no-path / 1 malformed / 0 missing-explicit), help/version output, bad-arg hint, and CliEnv plumbing (HOME/XDG precedence). Follow-up filed for run_with_segments_and_width stderr plumbing.

title: Warn on unknown keys in config.toml (not just silently ignore)
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) review: spec (docs/specs/config.md §Validation rules §1/§6) says unknown top-level keys should WARN and be ignored, and unknown keys in [segments.<id>] blocks should WARN and be ignored. The current impl silently ignores all unknown keys (no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] anywhere) because deny_unknown_fields rejected spec-valid forward-compat keys like 'theme', '$schema', 'layout'.

Correct fix requires a two-phase parse: first parse into a tolerant struct for backwards/forwards compat, then validate the raw toml::Value tree against a known-key allow-list and emit warnings. That's more work than this slice needed.

User impact today: typos like 'priorty = 10' silently drop instead of warning. Matters more once --check-config becomes a CI gate.
close_reason: Unknown-key warnings via two-phase parse (toml::Value → validate_keys → try_into). Allow-lists: top-level (implemented + spec-documented forward-compat), [layout_options] fields, per-segment schema that tightly gates built-ins while skipping unknown ids so plugins own their own schema. Warnings surface on render stderr and count toward --check-config summary. 17 new tests (281 lib + 7 integration).

title: Multi-line layout: [line.N] sections + layout="multi-line"
description:
Support multi-line status lines per docs/specs/config.md §Multi-line layouts.

Config shape:
- layout = "multi-line" at top level
- [line.1] segments = [...]
- [line.2] segments = [...]
Each line runs the layout algorithm independently, emits its own newline-terminated string.

Edge cases (from spec edge-case table):
- layout = "multi-line" with no [line.N] sections → treat as single-line, warn
- layout = "single-line" with [line.N] sections present → info log, use [line] for rendering
- [line] AND [line.N] both present → document precedence

Depends on lsm-u8u (config parser) and lsm-aql (layout engine — already shipped).

title: Color policy: --no-color / --force-color + NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR + [layout_options]
description:
Wire color emission through CLI flags, env vars, and config.

**Precedence (first match wins):**
1. `--no-color` or `--force-color` CLI flag
2. `NO_COLOR` env var (per no-color.org, any non-empty value)
3. `FORCE_COLOR` env var (any non-empty value)
4. `[layout_options].color = "auto"|"always"|"never"` in config
5. Default "auto" (TTY detection via supports-color)

**Also in this slice:**
- `[layout_options].claude_padding` — factored into width calc before handing to layout

**Out of scope (filed as follow-up):**
- `[layout_options].separator` styles (`powerline`, `capsule`, `flex`). Powerline needs Nerd Font glyph emission and affects layout-engine width math; capsule + flex are v0.2+ per spec. Separate bead.

Depends on lsm-u8u (config parser) and lsm-7kn (theme system — both shipped).
close_reason: Color policy precedence chain (CLI --no-color/--force-color > NO_COLOR env > FORCE_COLOR env > [layout_options].color > auto) + claude_padding width calc. FORCE_COLOR parses 0/false/off as 'absent' per npm/chalk convention. ColorPolicy, ColorOverride, LayoutOptions marked #[non_exhaustive]; LayoutOptions fields flattened (no redundant Option wrappers). 18 new tests (262 lib + 7 integration). Separator styles filed as lsm-1my (powerline needs Nerd Font emission; out of scope here).

title: Publish config.schema.json via schemars + CI drift check
description:
Derive a JSON Schema from the config.toml Rust types using schemars; commit config.schema.json at the repo root and embed via include_str! for offline editor integrations. CI fails when the committed schema is stale relative to the types (regenerate-and-diff check).

Editor integrations (taplo, VS Code, Zed) pick up the schema via the '$schema' key in the user's config, written by 'linesmith init' and 'linesmith presets apply'.

Depends on lsm-u8u (for the Config types to derive from). Dep: schemars.

title: linesmith presets list + presets apply + 5 embedded presets
description:
Part A of the original lsm-kb6 split (Part B = lsm-5yd for 'linesmith init' interactive onboarding).

**Scope:**
- 'linesmith presets list' — prints embedded preset names, one per line, in stable order
- 'linesmith presets apply <name>' — writes the preset's TOML body to the resolved config path:
  - If file exists: prompt 'overwrite config.toml? [y/N]' on stderr; on yes, back up existing as config.toml.bak (overwrite prior .bak if present); on no, abort with exit 1
  - '--force' flag skips prompt; still writes backup
  - If name is unknown: fail fast listing valid names, exit non-zero
  - Create parent directories as needed (0755)
- Unknown subcommand under 'presets' → clear error per the existing 'themes' dispatch pattern in cli.rs
- 5 embedded presets (include_str!) per docs/specs/config.md §Presets:
  - minimal: model + context_window
  - developer: model + workspace + git + context_window + cost + rate_limit_5h + rate_limit_7d
  - power-user: everything v0.1 supports (defer multi-line to lsm-bvu)
  - cost-focused: model + context_window + cost + rate_limit_5h + rate_limit_7d
  - worktree-heavy: model + workspace + git + context_window
  - (Note: git_branch segment isn't built yet — include TODO comment in affected presets; filed separately if needed)
- Tests:
  - Every embedded preset parses via Config::from_str without warnings
  - Every embedded preset produces a non-empty segment list via build_segments
  - 'presets list' prints all 5 names
  - 'presets apply <name>' to a temp path writes expected bytes; with existing file creates .bak
  - Unknown preset name errors with list
  - --force skips prompt (driver-level test with stdin closed)

**Depends on:** lsm-u8u (config core, already done — parser + registry + XDG resolver)

**Acceptance:** 'linesmith presets list' prints the 5 names. 'linesmith presets apply developer' writes a valid config.toml to the XDG path. Re-running with file present prompts, backs up to .bak, and writes new content on confirm. '--force' skips prompt. Resulting config round-trips through Config::from_str and produces the expected segment list.
close_reason: Presets list/apply subcommands + 5 embedded TOMLs (minimal, developer, power-user, cost-focused, worktree-heavy). --force confirms overwrite skip; existing .bak refused unless --force (Windows-safe pre-remove). --config threads through to the target path. Prompt + backup notifications on stderr, only final success on stdout. Two follow-ups filed (lsm-rd7 broken-pipe exit code, lsm-9j7 rename permission test).

title: Truncate highest-priority segment before dropping under width pressure
description:
From slice-4 Codex review: the layout engine drops segments whole once total_width exceeds terminal_width, even when a single over-wide segment (e.g. a long workspace name) could be truncated to fit. Result: `linesmith/very-long-feature-branch-name` on a 30-40 col terminal disappears rather than showing a truncated location.

Current design: width.max is an absolute cap applied in collect_items, unconditional on terminal width. That helps when a segment is pathologically wide but doesn't address "terminal is narrower than natural segment width."

Proposed: before dropping the currently-selected-to-drop segment, attempt to truncate it to (segment_width - (total_width - terminal_width)) cells. Only drop when truncation fails (e.g. resulting width below width.min, or segment has no truncatable text).

Requires spec update to docs/specs/segment-system.md §Layout algorithm. Likely needs a per-segment "truncatable: bool" or "min_useful_width" hint so segments like model/cost that shouldn't truncate opt out.

Once this lands, revisit whether built-in segments (workspace especially) should declare width.max at all — they may not need to.

title: Consider Segment::render -> Result<Option<RenderedSegment>, SegmentError>
description: From slice-4 type-design review: current Segment::render returns Option<RenderedSegment> where None means 'hide.' A plugin that fails to render (rhai error, missing field, arithmetic overflow) has no distinct signal — it vanishes indistinguishably from intentional hiding. Evaluate changing the trait to return Result so runtime errors propagate separately. This is a breaking change the moment a real plugin implements the trait, so decide before the plugin slice ships.
close_reason: Shipped in b36a638: Segment::render returns RenderResult = Result<Option<RenderedSegment>, SegmentError>; errors log to stderr and hide. 135 tests green.

title: Lock down RenderedSegment and SegmentDefaults public fields before plugin API
description: From slice-4 type-design review: RenderedSegment has pub text/width/right_separator; the invariant width == text_width(text) is load-bearing but only enforced at construction. Mutating .text silently desyncs width. Same concern on SegmentDefaults's pub fields — currently no builder beyond with_priority so plugin authors needing to set width/default_separator must use struct literal, blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. Options: make fields pub(crate) + add accessors, or add with_width/with_default_separator chainable builders. Decide before plugin runtime ships.
close_reason: Shipped in 3388b2a: RenderedSegment fields pub(crate) with getters, SegmentDefaults gains with_width/with_default_separator chainable builders.

title: Strip control characters from segment output to prevent terminal injection
description: From slice-4 silent-failure review: segment text can contain control chars (ESC, bell, etc.) which `UnicodeWidthChar::width` reports as 0 cells but are pushed into output verbatim. A malicious project dir at `~/work/evil\x1b[2J/` could blank the user terminal on every statusline render. Strip or escape control characters in RenderedSegment::new and/or text_width.
close_reason: Strip char::is_control() chars in RenderedSegment::new and with_separator. Fast no-alloc path when text is clean. Integration-level tests lock hostile project_dir and worktree name cases against regression.

title: Slice 5: File-based cache layer
description: Implement cache layer per docs/specs/segment-system.md. CachePolicy enum: AlwaysFresh, Ttl(Duration), Invalidated{any_of: Vec<CacheInvalidator>, ttl: Option<Duration>}. CacheInvalidator variants: FileChanged(PathBuf) via mtime, ContextFieldChanged(&'static str) via hash, SessionChanged. Storage: one file per segment under XDG_CACHE_HOME/linesmith/ with atomic temp-rename writes. Unlocks rate-limit scraping without blowing the <20ms budget.

title: Slice 3b: Tool detection heuristic + per-tool normalizer split
description: Split the inline claude module in input.rs into crates/linesmith/src/input/normalizers/{mod.rs,claude.rs,qwen.rs,other.rs}. Implement heuristic detection per input-schema.md (QwenCode if 'version' field present; ClaudeCode if 'cost.total_api_duration_ms' present; default ClaudeCode). Also lands the path_tail two-arg refactor from lsm-coc since the split multiplies the footgun.

title: Slice 3: CostMetrics + cost segment
description: Add CostMetrics{total_cost_usd: f64, total_duration_ms, total_api_duration_ms, total_lines_added, total_lines_removed} to StatusContext per ADR-0008. Implement cost segment rendering '$X.XX' using host-side format_cost_usd helper (per plugin-api.md contract). Claude normalizer maps 'cost' JSON object.

title: Slice 3: Effort segment
description: Add EffortLevel enum (Low/Medium/High/Max/XHigh) parsed from 'effort' field. Implement effort segment that renders the current /effort level when present. Claude Code doesn't emit this live today (per docs/research/user-demand.md ccstatusline#239) so the segment will be hidden in practice until Claude Code ships the re-emit; document this explicitly in the segment's doc comment.

title: Address Codex review: spec contract inconsistencies
description: 3 P2 inconsistencies: (1) format_cost_usd takes cents but ctx.cost.total_cost_usd is f64 dollars; (2) config.md visible_if uses nil but plugin-api says () is the sentinel; (3) plugin discovery precedence contradicts between plugin-api.md (plugin_dirs first) and config.md open question (default first).

(3) Plugin discovery precedence unified: plugin_dirs scanned first (project-local wins), default XDG scanned last. title: Add docs/research/README.md index

description: Currently bd init created both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with duplicate content. Goal: one source of truth with @import. Approach to evaluate: make AGENTS.md the source of truth (tool-agnostic convention) and have CLAUDE.md just @import it.
