If bd ever re-injects, run 'bd init --agents-file AGENTS.md' to redirect.

title: Add mise install:dev / install:release tasks for switching local linesmith binary
description:
Make the dev↔release toggle ergonomic: today we type cargo install --path ... by hand for dev mode, and there s no shortcut for testing as a user against the published binary. Add five mise tasks under the install: namespace.

Tasks:
- install:dev — cargo install --path crates/linesmith --locked --offline
- install:dev:checked — cargo check first, skip install on errors (typo fast-fail)
- install:release — cargo install linesmith --locked --force (latest crates.io)
- install:release:fast — fetch cargo-dist installer script (no compile)
- install:status — show shim path, reported version, mtime so user knows current state

Acceptance: mise tasks pass shellcheck, install:status correctly reports the binary mise shim resolves to, dev↔release switching works without PATH wrangling.
close_reason: Five mise tasks added under install: namespace. install:dev runs cargo install --path with --offline to skip registry refresh; install:dev:checked gates the slow install on cargo check passing first (typo fast-fail). install:release and install:release:fast cover the two release-mode paths (crates.io source compile vs. cargo-dist prebuilt binary). install:status shows shim path, version, and mtime so the active mode is unambiguous. Verified all 5 tasks load and install:status reports correctly against the current session's dev build.

title: Force-color fallthrough emits no observability when capability is downgraded
description:
Flagged by silent-failure-hunter review on 2026-04-24 (round 3). When a user sets `color = "always"` or `--force-color` and their effective capability gets downgraded (e.g. piped stdout + `TERM=xterm` with no COLORTERM → `Palette16` via the env probe), there's no visibility into WHY `force_color_detect` picked the tier it did.

Real risk: CI pipe with `TERM=xterm` gets ANSI SGR bytes in logs because the user asked for force-color and we floor at Palette16 — the user might not realize the floor is kicking in.

**Fix sketch:**
- Add an `lsm_debug!` or `lsm_warn!` with the resolved `(colorterm_raw, term_raw, tty_cap, env_cap, final_cap)` tuple when `force_color_detect` fires.
- Gate behind a debug-only log level (not stderr on every invocation) so the CC statusline doesn't go noisy.
- Consider: when `supports-color` returned None BECAUSE stdout isn't a TTY AND env probe also returned None, prefer `None` over the `Palette16` floor — but that changes semantics; worth discussion.

**Blocked by:** a debug-log sink design. Today there's no `lsm_debug!` macro reachable from this layer; warn goes to stderr which statusline users would find noisy.

**Acceptance:** a user running `LINESMITH_LOG=debug linesmith` with `--force-color` and a degraded env sees one stderr line explaining the tier choice; no log noise in the default path.

title: Consider (Percent, Clamp) enum return from Percent::from_f64_clamped
description:
Follow-up from lsm-mxcd review (silent-failure Important #1). The new `Percent::from_f64_clamped` returns `Option<Percent>`, making the clamp invisible to callers. The doc comment labels it "silent" and directs callers to emit diagnostics themselves, but that is a discipline tax — a future caller in a new parser path could clamp silently without a warn.

**Proposal:** change the signature to `fn from_f64_clamped(value: f64) -> Option<(Self, Clamp)>` where `Clamp` is an enum like `Unchanged | ClampedLow | ClampedHigh`. The compiler then forces callers to pattern-match and decide how to surface the clamp.

**Scope:** updates the clamped-constructor call site in `input.rs` and the inline clamps in `data_context/usage.rs:240-247, 254-262` (which could consolidate onto the helper). Small API change with a moderate call-site ripple.

**Why deferred:** the current fix in lsm-mxcd is a minimum-viable bug close; the API redesign is a separate quality improvement. Worth its own bead to keep the diff focused.

title: Add tolerance filter to the context_window.used_percentage clamp warn
description:
Follow-up from lsm-mxcd review (silent-failure Important #2). The current `lsm_warn!` in `parse_context_window` fires whenever `used_percentage` is outside [0, 100], with no tolerance. Claude Code invokes the statusline every ~300ms; on a persistent post-compact state this could produce ~200 warn lines/minute.

**Proposal:** only warn when the deviation exceeds a tolerance (e.g. |used_raw - clamp_bound| > 1.0). Tiny floating-point overshoot like 100.0000001 would clamp silently (correct: stdlib narrowing artifact). Real drift like 101.3 would still warn.

**Why deferred:** we don't know the actual magnitude of upstream drift yet. Calibrating the threshold now is speculative. Depends on live-test data from lsm-mdd7 (the captured stdin will show the real distribution of out-of-range values).

title: logging: add pub(crate) emit_to(level, msg, sink) for testable warn capture
description:
Current `logging::emit` writes straight to `io::stderr().lock()` with no injectable sink; only `emit_error_to` has one. Plugin-mirror tests can verify behavioral outcomes (truncated length, dropped keys) but cannot assert that the `lsm_warn!` side-effect actually fired. A mirror that silently removed its warn paths would pass every current test.

**Proposal:** mirror the `emit_error_to` pattern — add `pub(crate) fn emit_to(level: Level, msg: &str, sink: &mut dyn io::Write)` in `logging.rs`, swap the existing `emit` to delegate. Then add one warn-assertion test per cap in ctx_mirror's test module (depth, map, array, string, key-dropped).

**Context:** lsm-4c70 review (pr-test-analyzer gap #6). Cross-cuts logging.rs (outside ctx_mirror scope) so it was deferred from the original fix.

title: ctx_mirror: surface truncation as a first-class plugin signal (ctx.meta.truncated)
description:
Plugins currently cannot distinguish a genuinely-null JSON field from a host-side truncation (both mirror as rhai `()`), and a capped unknown_buckets map from a natively-256-entry one (both have len=256). The aggregated `lsm_warn!` is the only human signal; there is no machine-readable signal.

**Proposal (ADR-sized):** introduce a top-level `ctx.meta.truncated: [String]` (or structured Array) populated by the same ConversionLimits pass used for the warn. Plugins can read this to decide whether to render a 'partial data' indicator.

**Scope considerations:**
- Changes the plugin-api contract (new top-level `ctx.meta` namespace).
- Warrants an ADR before implementation — see docs/adrs/0000-template.md.
- Touches crates/linesmith/src/plugins/ctx_mirror.rs and docs/specs/plugin-api.md.

**Context:** lsm-4c70 review (code-reviewer #4, silent-failure-hunter #3). The `()`-for-truncation pattern was originally documented in the inline comment but the claim was factually wrong since `JsonValue::Null` shares the mapping; the comment has been corrected.

title: cascade: usage_error_from_code drops credential variant tags
description:
UsageError::code() delegates Credentials(...) to inner CredentialError::code(), emitting 'SubprocessFailed' / 'IoError' / 'MissingField' / 'EmptyToken' / 'ParseError'. None of these are matched in usage_error_from_code; all collapse to UsageError::NetworkError.

Unreachable today — cred errors short-circuit before any write_failure_lock call, and CachedUsage::with_error has no non-test caller for credential codes. But if a future change persists a credential-variant code (error cache, lock for cred fail, etc.), every credential failure renders [Network error] instead of the expected [Keychain error] / [No credentials] / etc.

Fix: extend the match to cover credential codes mapping back to UsageError::Credentials(...) — which is tricky because CredentialError inners are non-Clone. Alternative: add a debug_assert! on the fallback arm.

Found in lsm-xhu code review C1.

title: logging: warn on segments that can never render in current mode
description:
Under JSONL fallback, rate_limit_7d_reset and extra_usage hide unconditionally (7d has no hard reset; transcripts have no overage data). Today the hide sites log at debug level, consistent with the broader 'Ok(None) hides at debug' convention.

But there's a category difference: 5h/7d/5h-reset hide on *transient* sub-window conditions, while 7d-reset and extra_usage hide on a *configuration-mode mismatch* — the user configured a segment that cannot render in this fallback mode regardless of data. A user who loses their OAuth token and wonders why those two segments vanished while others survive needs LINESMITH_LOG=debug to find out.

Options: bump to warn unconditionally; gate on 'first time per process' to avoid spam; add a doctor-command surface instead. Found in lsm-xhu silent-failure review #3.

title: rate-limit: 401 + fresh-cache can hide revoked token for cache_duration
description:
When a token is revoked while the 180s endpoint cache is still fresh, the cascade returns cached Endpoint(...) on every invocation and never hits the 401-aware failure-lock path. Users see plausible-looking percent values for up to cache_duration seconds before the render flips to tokens/Unauthorized.

Self-correcting: once the cache goes stale, fetch → 401 → failure lock writes → flip to ~5h: 420k (JSONL) or [Unauthorized]. So this is a latency bug, not a correctness failure.

Mitigation: on the first 401, invalidate (or zero-TTL) the cache entry so peers see the transition immediately. Also update rate-limit-segments.md v0.2.1 changelog which overstates the 'every endpoint-failure path' claim.

Found during lsm-xhu review (code-reviewer I1).

title: Verify usageLimitResetTime semantic before consuming it in rate_limit_5h_reset
description:
Verify the semantic of Claude Code's `usageLimitResetTime` field in `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` records before wiring it into the `rate_limit_5h_reset` JSONL-mode render path.

Context: ADR-0013 chose `FiveHourWindow.ends_at` (= `block.start + 5h`, ccusage-style floor-to-hour) as the reset-timestamp source under JSONL. `FiveHourBlock.usage_limit_reset` remains on the aggregator but deliberately unconsumed by segments because the field's semantic is unverified. Research note `docs/research/jsonl-data-source.md` flags: "Claude Code may emit this only when the user has actually been rate-limited."

Open questions:
- When does Claude Code write the field? Every entry? Only on rate-limited interactions? Per-session or per-block?
- What timestamp does it represent — next 5h-window reset, 429 rate-limit lift, something else?
- Is the semantic stable across Claude Code versions?

Verification plan:
1. Collect a live JSONL sample by intentionally hitting a 429 during a Claude Code session.
2. Compare the timestamp to `block.start + 5h` and to any `retry-after` header visible on the 429.
3. Re-test on a non-rate-limited session: is the field present at all?
4. Cross-check against ccusage's consumer (`_session-blocks.ts`) to see what it assumes.

Outcome:
- If the field is the next 5h reset and is reliably present: wire it into `JsonlUsage` / `FiveHourWindow` as the primary source, fall back to `block.end()` when absent.
- If it's the 429 lift time: keep unconsumed; document clearly on `FiveHourBlock.usage_limit_reset`.
- If inconsistent or absent on most sessions: keep `block.end()` as the source; optionally surface `usage_limit_reset` as a separate "next deadline" signal in a new segment.

Dependencies: none (can be verified without code changes; update `jsonl-aggregation.md` and `ADR-0013` once confirmed).

title: Document logger-message convention + add lsm_debug_once! for steady-state gates
description:
Two related logger-surface refinements surfaced during the lsm-0cfx review. Both touch crates/linesmith/src/logging.rs; bundling so one bead covers the call-site grammar contract end-to-end.

Part A — Document the message convention:

- The lsm-cgg pattern `<segment-id>: <gate-condition>; hiding` is now replicated at 17 call sites (rate-limit segments + cost/effort/context_window/git_branch/workspace). Nothing in code or spec captures the grammar, so the next contributor mimics whatever string they happen to read first.
- Add a "Segment diagnostic convention" paragraph to logging.rs module docs (or a short section in docs/specs/segment-system.md) naming:
  - The `<segment-id>: <gate>; hiding` shape.
  - The `absent` / `in the past` vocabulary distinction (None vs present-but-invalid).
  - When to include a parenthetical value (present-but-invalid payload worth surfacing, e.g. `resets_at in the past ({resets_at})`).
  - When to escalate to lsm_warn! (gate isn't a normal hide but a structural oddity).

Part B — lsm_debug_once! dedup:

- A user who opts into LINESMITH_LOG=debug on an API-tier Claude Code session will see three lines per invocation (context_window absent, cost absent, effort absent) at a 300ms CC debounce. That's roughly 10 lines/sec sustained; no new information after the first emission.
- Proposed knob: lsm_debug_once!(key, "<msg>") where `key` is a &'static str label (e.g. "cost:status.cost-absent"). First fire-per-process emits; subsequent fires with the same key silently drop. Reuses the existing LINESMITH_LOG gate.
- State store: a `OnceLock<Mutex<HashSet<&'static str>>>` or similar; negligible runtime cost.
- Migration: swap the 4 CC-null hide sites (context_window, cost, effort, plus the 2 rate_limit_*_reset `absent` gates) to `lsm_debug_once!`. Leave dynamic gates (`resets_at in the past ({resets_at})`) on `lsm_debug!` because the printed value carries signal.

Acceptance:
- Part A: logging.rs module doc names the convention. New contributors can read the docs and write a correct call-site without studying existing emissions.
- Part B: `cargo run` against a CC-null payload emits each null-gate debug line exactly once per process. Hot-path allocations remain zero when debug is suppressed.

Out of scope: doctor buffering (lsm-l35), hide-reason channel (lsm-45gx) — both orthogonal concerns.

title: Annotate remaining non-rate-limit segment Ok(None) hide paths
description:
Second follow-up from lsm-cgg (after lsm-awqz). The rate-limit Ok(None) hide paths got lsm_debug! annotations in lsm-cgg; the non-rate-limit segments have equivalent hide branches that were left bare. Annotate them so LINESMITH_LOG=debug explains every silent segment uniformly.

Sites to annotate:
- crates/linesmith/src/segments/context_window.rs:20 — status.context_window absent (null before first API call per the Claude Code statusline contract).
- crates/linesmith/src/segments/cost.rs:17 — status.cost absent (API-tier users never receive cost).
- crates/linesmith/src/segments/effort.rs:24 — status.effort unset (only set when the user picks one via /effort).
- crates/linesmith/src/segments/git_branch.rs:240 — RepoKind::Bare hide (already has an inline comment; promote to lsm_debug! for consistency).

Out of scope (deliberately leave bare):
- workspace.rs:34 — rare project_dir == "/" edge; self-explanatory from context.
- model.rs:17 — empty-after-trim defensive guard; unreachable against real Claude Code payloads.
- git_branch.rs:236, :244 — Err(_) | Ok(None) fallthrough (data layer already logs) and empty-assembled-text guard (defensive; impossible in practice).

Acceptance:
- Each of the 4 sites emits lsm_debug!("<segment>: <gate>; hiding") in the same prefix style as the rate-limit annotations from lsm-cgg.
- LINESMITH_LOG=debug output is now grep-complete: every default-line segment hide path has a corresponding log line.
- No behavior change at Warn (default); no new tests needed beyond the existing hide-path unit tests.
close_reason: 4 non-rate-limit segment hide paths now emit lsm_debug! using the same <segment>: <gate>; hiding convention as lsm-cgg: context_window (status.context_window absent), cost (status.cost absent), effort (status.effort unset), git_branch (RepoKind::Bare). LINESMITH_LOG=debug is now grep-complete across the default line. Deliberately left bare: workspace root-path edge, model empty-after-trim guard, git_branch not-a-repo/empty-text defensive paths.

title: Migrate ambient-stderr diagnostics to the lsm_warn! logger
description:
Follow-up from lsm-cgg. The in-crate logger landed with 12 initial call sites, but 5+ older diagnostics still write to ambient fd 2 via `let _ = writeln!(io::stderr().lock(), ...)` or `eprintln!`. Route them through `lsm_warn!` so `LINESMITH_LOG=off` can suppress them and so the emit format is uniform across the crate.

Sites to migrate:
- crates/linesmith/src/layout.rs:23 — layout-engine warn helper.
- crates/linesmith/src/lib.rs:153 — COLUMNS env-parse warning emitted by detect_terminal_width.
- crates/linesmith/src/data_context/mod.rs:253 — gix discovery failure (added in lsm-sog).
- crates/linesmith/src/data_context/git.rs — dirty-scan and upstream-resolution failures (two sites in the dirty() / upstream() accessors).
- crates/linesmith/src/plugins/engine.rs:236 — plugin runtime diagnostic. Preserve the existing rate-limit counter (see lines 212 rationale) when wrapping.

Out of scope (do NOT migrate):
- Anything in driver.rs flowing through the injected stderr: &mut dyn Write parameter — that's CLI subcommand output, not diagnostic logging. Routing through lsm_warn! would bypass the injection contract and regress test isolation.
- lib.rs:120,131 parse error + run_with_context writes — they take stderr as a parameter; leave them.

Acceptance:
- All five sites write via crate::lsm_warn! (or lsm_debug! where appropriate).
- LINESMITH_LOG=off suppresses every one of them.
- No regressions in existing test output; the "linesmith: parse:" marker lines in the integration suite stay as they are.
- Format uniformity: every migrated site produces `linesmith [warn]: <message>` rather than mixing prefixes.

Deferred to later:
- Buffering for linesmith doctor surface — picked up when lsm-l35 lands.
close_reason: 5 diagnostic sites migrated off ambient writeln!(io::stderr()) / eprintln! to the crate logger: layout.rs warn helper, lib.rs COLUMNS parse warning (detect_terminal_width), data_context::mod.rs git discovery failure, data_context::git.rs dirty-scan + upstream-resolution + upstream-refname warnings, plugins::engine.rs plugin log() (per-plugin rate-limit counter preserved). LINESMITH_LOG=off now suppresses every diagnostic. Driver subcommand output (help/version/presets/init/check-config) deliberately left on the injected stderr sink per the CliEnv injection contract.

title: Hide-reason channel for segments: distinguish 'no data' from 'intentionally hidden'
description:
Silent-failure-hunter flagged during lsm-cgg review: Segment::render returning Ok(None) conflates 'data missing' (e.g. rate_limits absent, cost unset) with 'intentionally hidden' (e.g. visible_if condition false). The new LINESMITH_LOG=debug diagnostics expose the gate, but users who configured a segment to always render something see nothing in-band.

**Scope:**
- Extend Segment::render return type with a hide-reason enum (e.g. Ok(Render::Shown(r)) / Ok(Render::Hidden(HideReason))), or add a HideReason channel on the existing Ok(None) path via a struct return.
- Users can opt into a placeholder render via config, e.g. [segments.rate_limit_5h] on_missing = 'show-placeholder' -> renders '[no 5h data]'.
- Migrate the 8 Ok(None) sites touched by lsm-cgg plus any older ones to produce structured hide reasons instead of bare None.

**Why:**
- Observability complaint: user sets LINESMITH_LOG=debug just to see why their statusline is blank; in-band placeholder removes the need.
- Test determinism: 'no data' vs 'disabled' are distinct test invariants; conflating them makes segment tests fuzzy.

**Depends on:** lsm-l35 (doctor) if doctor is the primary surface for hide reasons; otherwise none.

**Not in scope:**
- Changing the rendered output semantics for segments that currently hide silently on 'no data' — behavior preserved by default, placeholder is opt-in.

**Driven by:** silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-cgg (2026-04-22).

title: Criterion bench for git-segments perf budget (<5ms warm, <15ms cold)
description:
Spec  declares a <5ms warm / <15ms cold render budget for every git-derived segment (git_branch and friends). The v0.1 git epic (lsm-8jl) shipped without a pinned benchmark — acceptance relies on inspection, not measurement.

**Scope:**
- Add crates/linesmith/benches/git_segments.rs (criterion).
- Cold: fresh DataContext against a tempdir repo (one seed commit, no upstream). Assert p95 < 15ms.
- Warm: second access through the same DataContext (OnceCell hit). Assert effectively zero-cost.
- Large-repo dirty-scan fast path: 10k-file tempdir, indicator mode. Assert short-circuit keeps p95 < 5ms.
- Include fixture for a linked worktree so workspace's new ctx.git() read doesn't regress.

**Depends on:** none (reuses existing gix fixture helpers in data_context::git tests and the run_git helper in tests/integration.rs).

**Acceptance:** `cargo bench -p linesmith --bench git_segments` passes locally and the numbers are recorded in the bench's own criterion output; failing thresholds abort the bench run.

title: compute_upstream: error-path tests
description:
compute_upstream returns Ok(None) for several benign-error cases and bubbles others, but none of the error / partial-config paths are exercised by tests:

- configured-but-unfetched (branch.main.remote=origin; branch.main.merge=refs/heads/never-fetched; no .git/refs/remotes/origin/never-fetched) → Ok(None)
- remote_tracking_ref_name returning Some(Err(_)) → Err bubbles
- peel_to_id_in_place failure on symbolic upstream pointing at missing ref → Err bubbles
- shallow repo → Ok(None) via is_shallow short-circuit

Each can be tested via the run_git / fixture_with_upstream helpers with specific git config.

title: count_ancestors_excluding: direct tests on merge graphs
description:
count_ancestors_excluding in data_context/git.rs is the heart of the flake-free ahead/behind count. Covered transitively through upstream_reports_* but no direct unit tests. Mutation testing would pass against current fixtures for several wrong implementations.

Add:
- count_ancestors_excluding_returns_zero_when_tip_equals_stop
- count_ancestors_excluding_on_linear_history (tip == 3 commits past stop → 3)
- count_ancestors_excluding_on_merge_graph (feature branch merged back into main; walk from main HEAD with merge_base as stop should count correctly with shared branch history)

Reuses the fixture_with_upstream helpers.

title: UpstreamState plugin mirror: structured WalkerFailed variant
description:
Today GitContext::upstream() collapses four states into Arc<None>: (1) HEAD not on branch, (2) no tracking remote, (3) tracking ref missing, (4) walker failed partway. Plugin code reading ctx.git.data.upstream can't distinguish case 4 from cases 1-3, so any plugin UI that says 'run git branch --set-upstream-to' shows that message even on gix panic.

Current fix: docstring explicitly documents the fusion. Real fix: add UpstreamStatus enum { NoUpstream, Ok(UpstreamState), Failed { message } } or plumb Arc<Result<Option<UpstreamState>, GitError>> through the OnceCell. Plays well with lsm-cgg (structured logger) since we'd have a typed error to emit.

Scope: data_context/git.rs OnceCell shape + plugin ctx_mirror output + segment render match.

title: git_branch: truncate_middle coverage for CJK + combining graphemes
description:
truncate_middle in segments/git_branch.rs is grapheme-aware and width-aware, but tests only cover ASCII. Missing coverage:

- Wide (CJK / emoji) graphemes where cells ≠ chars ≠ bytes (e.g. branch 'feature/日本語-123')
- Combining sequences (e.g. 'e\u{0301}' = é as two code points, one grapheme)
- Asymmetric head/tail budget with odd total — pin the head-biased ceil/floor split
- Boundary: marker_width exactly equals max budget

Current ASCII-only tests would pass if someone accidentally swapped UnicodeWidthStr::width for .len(). Add the cases from the pr-test-analyzer finding #5.

title: git_branch: linked-worktree render path + tests
description:
lsm-4cf landed RepoKind::LinkedWorktree classification in data_context/git.rs but never exercised the linked-worktree path end-to-end. Spec §Edge cases table lists linked worktree as in-scope for v0.1.

**Scope:**
- Unit test for resolve_repo on a hand-built linked worktree fixture (see pr-test-analyzer recipe: fabricate .git/worktrees/<name>/ directory with HEAD, commondir, gitdir files + .git file in the worktree checkout)
- Integration test exercising git_branch render through cli_main against a linked worktree cwd
- Verify the per-worktree branch (not the main checkout's) is rendered
- Confirm classify_kind returns LinkedWorktree { name } with the correct basename

title: git_branch: detect HEAD↔index (staged-only) dirty changes
description:
gix 0.67's public API doesn't expose a HEAD→index diff (per their own TODO on `Repository::is_dirty`). Our current dirty scan catches untracked + worktree-vs-index modifications but misses the case where a user has run `git add` and then immediately checks the statusline — the staged change is in the index but not yet committed, and there's no worktree modification to catch it with index-worktree scan alone.

**Scope:**
- Compare HEAD's root tree OID against the current index's would-be tree OID (via cache-tree extension if valid, otherwise compute)
- Short-circuit early in fast-path (indicator) mode once any difference is detected
- Add to `compute_dirty` in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/git.rs
- Test fixture: repo with one committed file, `git add foo.rs` (new file added to index), assert dirty
- May require upgrading to a newer gix once it ships the tree-index diff API

**Why this matters:** dirty indicator is on-by-default; users who `git add foo` and see clean statusline will be misled. Known limitation documented in git-segments.md v0.1.1 changelog.

title: Config validator: nested-table key allow-lists
description:
The config::segment_override_schema allow-list is shallow — it only validates direct children of [segments.<id>]. Nested tables like [segments.git_branch.dirty] pass all keys silently, so a typo in 'indicator' vs 'indictor' won't warn.

**Why this matters:** the git_branch spec has a non-trivial nested schema (branch.*, dirty.*, ahead_behind.*) and users benefit from same-quality validation as the top-level keys.

**Scope:**
- Extend validate_segments_table to walk one level deeper
- Per-id nested allow-lists — git_branch.dirty, git_branch.branch, git_branch.ahead_behind (when lsm-7o7 lands)
- Tests per table: unknown nested key emits a warning naming the path (e.g. 'unknown key X in [segments.git_branch.dirty]; ignoring')
- Keep shallow behavior for plugin segments (unknown id → skip validation)

Filed during lsm-4cf — today nested keys pass through silently and users only find out by the segment ignoring their knob.

title: git_branch: counts-mode dirty scan (staged/unstaged/untracked split)
description:
The [segments.git_branch] dirty.format = 'counts' knob parses successfully but warns and falls back to 'indicator' mode because the full scan isn't wired yet. lsm-4cf landed only the fast-path is_dirty() call that sets DirtyState.any.

**Scope:**
- Populate DirtyState.staged / unstaged / untracked via gix::Repository::status_platform with a full scan
- Decide on TTL caching across invocations (spec §Open questions notes this)
- Gate behind the dirty-counts renderer so repos that don't need counts still pay only is_dirty()
- Remove the 'counts is not yet implemented' warning in segments/git_branch.rs from_extras
- Tests: fixtures with 1 staged, 1 unstaged, 1 untracked — render counts-mode output per spec §Render examples

**Depends on:** lsm-4cf (git_branch base segment).

**Spec reference:** docs/specs/git-segments.md §Dirty detection strategy.

title: Integration test: TOML config → build_segments → rate-limit render
description:
The per-segment `from_extras_*` unit tests (lsm-7po) and the `segment_override_schema` allow-list tests each cover their piece, but there's no integration test for the full pipeline:

1. Load a `[segments.rate_limit_5h] format = "progress"` config via `Config::from_str_validated`
2. `build_segments` dispatches to `built_in_by_id("rate_limit_5h", Some(&extras), warn)`
3. `from_extras` applies the knobs
4. Segment renders with progress-bar output (block chars, not "22.0%")

A regression where `built_in_by_id` drops the extras arg on ONE rate-limit segment (refactor error) would leave knobs silently inert — the unit tests wouldn't fire, `validate_keys` wouldn't fire, segment would render with defaults.

Write one integration test per segment family (5h/7d, reset, extra_usage = 3 tests) using `DataContext::preseed_usage` so the test doesn't hit real Keychain/network. Add to `crates/linesmith/tests/integration.rs`.

title: Test: pin every UsageSource variant → snake_case mirror string
description:
`build_usage_data` in `plugins/ctx_mirror.rs` (lsm-7po) converts `UsageSource::{Endpoint, Jsonl}` → `"endpoint"` / `"jsonl"` via an exhaustive match. Parallel to the existing `all_tool_variants_map_to_snake_case_kind` test that pins every `Tool` variant, we should pin every `UsageSource` variant so an accidental label rename surfaces in CI.

Smaller than it sounds: just a table-driven test with 2 rows today (`Endpoint`, `Jsonl`). When a third variant lands (cached/composite/etc. per lsm-xhu and future work), the test forces an update to both the match and its plugin-facing label contract.

title: Enrich TOML parse warn messages with observed type hints
description:
The `parse_bool` / `parse_percent_format` / `parse_duration_format` / `parse_extra_usage_format` helpers in `segments/rate_limit_format.rs` currently collapse wrong-type and unknown-value errors into one message ("expected X or Y; ignoring").

A user who typed `invert = 1` (common JSON-mental-model mistake) sees the same "expected bool" message as someone who typed `invert = "true"`. Including `toml::Value::type_str()` in the warn text turns "I don't know what I did wrong" into "I wrote an integer where a bool belongs."

Apply across:
- `parse_bool` (invert, compact, use_days)
- `parse_percent_format`
- `parse_duration_format`
- `parse_extra_usage_format`
- `apply_common_extras` (icon, label, stale_marker, progress_width — 4 sites)

Also split `format` parsers so wrong-type and unknown-enum-value emit distinct messages. Estimate: ~50 LOC + test updates.

title: Spec: document UsageError::Jsonl rendering in rate-limit-segments.md error table
description:
`rate_limit_format::render_error` (lsm-7po) maps `UsageError::Jsonl(NoEntries|DirectoryMissing)` → `[No data]` and other `Jsonl(_)` → `[Parse error]` but `docs/specs/rate-limit-segments.md` §Error message table doesn't document either mapping.

Consequences:
- A plugin author reading the spec can't predict what string a JSONL failure produces
- The `[Parse error]` collapse for `JsonlError::IoError` misleadingly tells users it's a JSON syntax issue when it's a filesystem error
- The current comment at `rate_limit_format.rs:~293` acknowledges `doctor` carries the detail, but doctor wiring isn't landed (see lsm-cgg)

Action:
- Amend §Error message table with rows for JSONL variants (NoEntries, DirectoryMissing → `[No data]`; IoError, ParseError → decide between `[No data]` / `[Parse error]` / a new bucket like `[Transcript error]`)
- Update `render_error` to match the amended spec (code change likely trivial once spec lands)
- Add test rows to `error_rendering_covers_spec_table`

title: jsonl aggregator: structured diagnostics for silent-skip paths when logger lands
description:
Silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-26y flagged three silent-skip paths in the JSONL aggregator that are spec-correct (per §Edge cases) but invisible when debugging:

1. `JsonlTailer::read_new` drops malformed JSON lines silently (line 317-319 of jsonl.rs). The offset advances past them so they never re-parse, but there is no counter, no path-recording, no hook for linesmith doctor.
2. `collect_from_root` swallows per-file `tailer.read_new()` errors with `let Ok(file_entries) = ... else { continue }` (line 392-394). Permission-denied / IO corruption on a single transcript → file disappears from aggregation AND from source_paths. No forensic trail.
3. `collect_from_root` swallows per-project `read_dir` errors with `match ... Err(_) => continue` (line 382-385). Asymmetric with top-level `read_dir(root)` which properly surfaces JsonlError::IoError.
4. `.flatten()` calls on ReadDir iterators (lines 377, 386) silently drop per-entry Err variants.

Scope: when a structured logger lands in linesmith (natural companion to lsm-l35 doctor), add logForDebugging / logError calls in each of these paths, plus a `skipped_paths: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>` and `skipped_malformed: u64` on JsonlAggregate so linesmith doctor can report them.

Acceptance: corrupt-transcript or unreadable-project-dir scenarios produce actionable log lines; linesmith doctor can surface them to the user.
design: Deferred from lsm-26y because linesmith has no structured logger yet. Same logger-dependent pattern as lsm-038 (cache + lock) and lsm-6wx (UsageError taxonomy). All three likely get addressed together when the logger lands.

title: Lock wire format: add schema_version for future-compat
description:
LockStore::read currently routes any JSON that does not match the Lock shape into the legacy-mtime fallback. Silent-failure-hunter flagged this as a latent compat risk: if a future linesmith writes a new Lock shape (e.g. adds fields), todays binary will treat that file as a legacy plaintext lock and synthesize mtime+30s, ignoring the real blocked_until.

Scope: add schema_version: u32 to Lock; distinguish "old plaintext lock" (no braces, parse to legacy) from "newer-schema JSON lock" (has braces but wrong shape, surface as CacheError). First-byte sniff (if it is `{`, treat parse failure as real error) would work as a lighter alternative.

Acceptance: future lock schema changes are distinguishable from legacy plaintext; todays readers emit a clear error when they encounter an unknown future JSON shape rather than silently degrading.
design: Deferred from lsm-b9w because the v0.1 lock shape is frozen and the risk only fires when we do a schema rev. Low priority until we actually have a reason to change the format.

title: cache + lock: emit structured diagnostics when logging layer lands
description:
CacheStore::read (and LockStore::read) currently collapse several conditions into Ok(None) silently: schema_version mismatch, clock skew, malformed JSON on our own file, legacy non-JSON lock fallback. Silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-b9w flagged that a corrupt usage.json written by our own atomic_write_json will be silently overwritten on the next successful fetch, erasing the forensic trail.

Scope: when a structured logger lands in linesmith, add logForDebugging calls in:
1. CacheStore::read match fallthrough — distinguish schema_version / clock_skew / parse_error with dedicated log calls
2. LockStore::read legacy-fallback branch — log that we routed an un-parseable JSON file through the mtime+30s path
3. cap_blocked_until — log when we cap a pathological blocked_until value
4. Lock mtime-pre-1970 case — log instead of silent unreachable

Acceptance: corrupt-cache conditions produce actionable log lines; operators can distinguish "cache never hit" root causes without attaching a debugger.
design: Deferred from lsm-b9w because linesmith has no structured logger yet. Natural companion to lsm-l35 (doctor) which will need similar diagnostic surfaces. Defensive coding has been added in the form of debug_assert for the mtime-pre-1970 case.

title: fetcher: real-transport integration tests (mockito/wiremock)
description:
Pr-test-analyzer review of lsm-7xv flagged that the entire UreqTransport impl is unreachable from the current test surface — the UsageTransport trait hides headers, so User-Agent and anthropic-beta header contracts are unit-tested only at the string-construction level (default_user_agent), not at the wire level.

Scope: add a mockito (or wiremock) dev-dep + integration tests under tests/ureq_transport_integration.rs that:
1. Stand up a mock server echoing requests
2. Call UreqTransport::get() against the mock
3. Assert headers (User-Agent format, anthropic-beta value, Authorization bearer), timeout enforcement, redirect handling, actual http_status_as_error(false) behavior
4. Catch ureq-3.x API drift in minor version bumps

Acceptance: headers are wire-tested, not merely format-tested. Ureq API regressions surface as test failures.
design: Deferred from lsm-7xv because: (a) mockito/wiremock is a new dev dep of non-trivial size, (b) the macOS PATH-injection pattern in lsm-yq8 uses similar integration-test scaffolding and could share setup, (c) unit tests cover the critical header-format contract via default_user_agent. Consider consolidating with lsm-yq8 if both land in the same release window.

title: UsageError taxonomy: split NetworkError into DNS / TLS / ConnectionRefused / BadUri
description:
Silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-7xv flagged that ureq_err_to_io currently fire-hoses every non-timeout variant (DNS failure, TLS handshake failure, invalid URI, connection refused, decompression error, protocol error) into UsageError::NetworkError. Users chasing a TLS cert expiry vs a DNS failure vs a mistyped api_base_url get no signal beyond "[Network error]".

Scope: widen UsageError with distinct variants (e.g. Dns, Tls, InvalidUrl, ConnectionRefused) or carry a Cow<str> detail on NetworkError. Map ureq::Error::{ConnectionFailed, Tls, BadUri, Io(kind)} → specific variants. Update docs/specs/rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table with new render strings. Update rate-limit segment renderer (lsm-7po) to handle new variants.

Acceptance: linesmith doctor can distinguish DNS failure from TLS failure from connection refused. Segment render strings cover each case.
design: Deferred from lsm-7xv because adding UsageError variants requires spec amendment (rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table) and a segment-renderer update (lsm-7po dependency). Current code is spec-compliant; richer diagnostics are v0.2 polish per ADR-0011 confirmation criterion.

title: plugin-api.md: add MissingField + EmptyToken to ctx.usage.error enumerated list
description:
plugin-api.md §ctx shape exposed to rhai enumerates ctx.usage.error as one of: "NoCredentials" | "SubprocessFailed" | "IoError" | "Timeout" | "RateLimited" | "NetworkError" | "ParseError" | "Unauthorized". Missing from that list: "MissingField" and "EmptyToken" which CredentialError produces and surfaces via UsageError::Credentials(...).code() delegation.

Scope: one-line spec update to add the two codes to the enumerated list. Cross-link from rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table (which already renders them as [Credentials corrupt]).

Acceptance: spec enumerated list matches what CredentialError::code() can produce; rhai plugins have a complete switch-arm list.
design: Lightweight. Can fold into the broader plugin-api.md v0.2 rev (lsm-7n2) rather than shipping as its own edit.

title: Refine `security` subprocess exit-code handling: errSecItemNotFound vs locked keychain
description:
The credential reader (crates/linesmith/src/data_context/credentials.rs:macos mod) currently collapses any non-zero `security find-generic-password` exit to Ok(None) (fall-through-to-next-step). This masks "Keychain locked" / "user denied access" / "binary not on PATH" as "no item found."

Scope: inspect ExitStatus.code() for `errSecItemNotFound = 44` — that status is the only one that should fall through. Any other non-zero exit should route to CredentialError::SubprocessFailed with stderr captured for `linesmith doctor`.

Acceptance: distinguishable error strings when the Keychain is locked vs empty; `linesmith doctor` reports actionable diagnostics matching the real failure mode.
design: Flagged by silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-a7a. Deferred because getting exit-code semantics exactly right requires inspecting the macOS SDK headers for non-44 codes that also mean "item not found" (unlikely but worth verifying). Needs a macOS reviewer with Keychain access.
close_reason: Subsumed by lsm-a7a: exit-code classification + 2s timeout landed in macos::classify_security_exit and macos::run_security during Codex review response. errSecItemNotFound (44) falls through; other non-zero exits route to SubprocessFailed with stderr captured. Timeout kills via deadline-polled try_wait. Unit tests cover the classifier via ExitStatusExt::from_raw.

title: macOS Keychain integration test via PATH-injected fake security binary
description:
Bead lsm-a7a acceptance called for injecting a fake `security` binary on PATH and asserting the primary path / multi-account fallback / mdat sort. lsm-a7a shipped only the `dump-keychain` output parser as unit tests — the orchestration layer (try_keychain_primary, try_keychain_multi_account, the cascade SubprocessFailed path in resolve_credentials) is untested end-to-end.

Scope: add an #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] integration test module under crates/linesmith/src/data_context/credentials.rs or tests/ that:
1. Creates a tempdir with a shell script named `security` that echoes controlled stdout based on argv
2. Prepends the tempdir to PATH for the test subprocess
3. Invokes resolve_credentials() and asserts the right branch fires (primary hit, multi-account mdat-newest wins, SubprocessFailed bubbles when both Keychain arms fail AND file cascade yields nothing)

Acceptance: primary-hit, multi-account-mdat-sort, and SubprocessFailed-preferred-over-NoCredentials are all covered. Fake binary is torn down cleanly. Tests skip on non-macOS via #[cfg].
design: Why deferred: PATH injection requires process-level env mutation during test execution; combined with the crate-level `unsafe_code = "forbid"` lint it needs careful scaffolding. Not a correctness blocker — the parser is unit-tested, the cascade plumbing is unit-testable via the FileCascadeEnv pattern, and production failure modes degrade visibly. Worth doing but should not block y6m slice progress.

title: Fix bd preflight config: references Go toolchain in a Rust project
description:
bd preflight output references go test, golangci-lint, gofmt, go.sum, vendorHash, version.go — none of which apply. linesmith is a Rust project using cargo + clippy + rustfmt (see AGENTS.md §Tooling).

Needs the beads preflight config (likely .beads/config or equivalent) updated to reference mise run check / mise run test / cargo fmt / cargo clippy and drop the Nix/Go checks. Investigate where beads stores this config first.
design: Likely lives in .beads/config.yml or equivalent. If the config is not user-editable (hard-coded beads defaults), file upstream with the beads project. If user-editable, one-line fix.
acceptance_criteria: bd preflight output matches the actual linesmith toolchain (cargo + mise). No references to Go, Nix, or Dolt-go tooling. AGENTS.md §Tooling table is the source of truth for what checks should appear.

title: Update plugin-api.md spec to v0.2 for segment trait v0.3
description:
segment-system.md v0.3 moved Segment::render from &StatusContext to &DataContext and added data_deps(). plugin-api.md still reflects the older trait contract. segment-system.md §Plugin wrapper explicitly flags this as a follow-up bead.

Needed: update RhaiSegment wrapper section to reflect ctx: &DataContext + data_deps; spell out the @data_deps script header parser contract (referenced in segment-system.md but defined here); update the rhai-side API for reading DataContext fields (ctx.usage, ctx.credentials with tagged-map error mirror per existing pattern).
design: Credential source is NOT plugin-accessible per data-fetching.md §DataDep — script header parser rejects "credentials" as a dep (already enforced in code per epic description). Spec needs to match.
acceptance_criteria: plugin-api.md rev to v0.2 with change-log entry; segment-system.md §Plugin wrapper drops the "follow-up bead" note.
notes: Additional scope: audit the rhai ctx mirror (plugin-api.md §ctx shape) for ctx.rate_limits references. After lsm-7po drops the stdin rate_limits path, plugins using ctx.rate_limits will break. Spec must document the migration (ctx.usage replaces ctx.rate_limits with the 8-variant tagged-map error shape documented in plugin-api.md §tagged-map error mirror). Include migration note in change-log.

title: Add typical.rhai bench fixture exercising ctx_mirror + host fns
description: The Phase 7 plugin_render_cold/warm benches use minimal.rhai which returns a literal map with no ctx access and no host-fn calls. ADR-0004 budgets are meant to survive a typical plugin reading ctx fields and calling format_tokens / format_duration. Add a typical.rhai fixture that exercises ctx_mirror::build_ctx (e.g. reads ctx.status.model.display_name, ctx.status.context_window.used) and host-fn dispatch (format_tokens), then add plugin_render_cold_typical / plugin_render_warm_typical benches alongside the minimal ones. Baseline numbers go in the commit message.

title: Tighten @data_deps header parser to match only declarations, not prose mentions
description: The header parser at crates/linesmith/src/plugins/header.rs substring-finds '@data_deps' anywhere inside the first contiguous //-comment block. A plugin author writing prose like '// no @data_deps header here' or '// see @data_deps spec' before any real declaration triggers a MalformedDataDeps load error because the matched substring lacks the expected '='. Bit us once during Phase 6 fixture authoring (minimal.rhai had prose mentioning the symbol in backticks). Fix: require the @data_deps token to appear at the start of a comment line (after the // and optional whitespace), not anywhere in the line. Add a fixture-or-unit-test pinning that prose mentions are ignored when no real declaration exists. Acceptance: a fixture with prose  parses cleanly with the default Status-only deps.

title: Plugin segments cannot replace built-ins by id
description: Today the registry rejects any plugin whose const ID matches a built-in (BUILT_IN_SEGMENT_IDS). A user who wants to ship their own model/workspace/cost segment can't, even with config opt-in. Decide: (a) keep current strict rejection (b) allow plugin override via opt-in flag like priority list (c) namespace plugins (e.g. const ID = "my.model"). Spec docs/specs/plugin-api.md does not currently address this.

title: Reconcile plugin role list: spec enumerates 15, code accepts 16 (background)
description:
plugin-api.md §Plugin return shape (around line 262-265) enumerates valid role tokens for a plugin's render() return: foreground | muted | primary | accent | success | warning | error | info | success_dim | warning_dim | error_dim | primary_dim | accent_dim | surface | border — 15 names.

crates/linesmith/src/plugins/output.rs:parse_role() also accepts "background", mapping it to Role::Background, because the Rust enum has all 16 variants and Role::Surface falls back to Role::Background internally.

Decide:
1. Add "background" to the spec's role list so the two agree.
2. Drop "background" from parse_role() and reject it as an unknown role.

Option 1 is likely correct (Role::Background is a real variant and the theme fallback chain uses it), but the spec is source of truth; pick one.

**Acceptance:** spec role list and plugins/output.rs parse_role match exactly.

title: Add end-to-end plugin flow integration test (config → discovery → registry → lookup)
description:
Phase 3 unit-tests each layer (18 header, 10 discovery, 12 registry tests) but no single test wires the whole chain: user Config.plugin_dirs → scan_plugin_dirs → PluginRegistry::load → reg.get(id) for a realistic multi-dir, multi-plugin, collision-containing layout.

Belongs in crates/linesmith/tests/integration.rs or a new tests/plugins.rs. Pair with the RhaiSegment wrapper (Phase 4) since the end-to-end value of this test is 'plugin is registered AND reachable by the render path' — RhaiSegment is what makes the second half true.

**Acceptance:** a test fixtures two dirs each with one plugin, one collision, and one bad plugin; asserts PluginRegistry::load registers the two good plugins in declaration order, reports the collision + compile error, and get() returns the right plugin.
close_reason: End-to-end plugin test landed: tests/integration.rs::xdg_plugin_renders_via_full_driver_path drives cli_main → load_plugins → build_segments → RhaiSegment::render with a real .rhai file under XDG.

title: Resolve 0-byte plugin file spec vs impl discrepancy
description:
plugin-api.md:448 §Edge cases: 'Plugin file is 0 bytes → Compiled as a no-op AST; render call returns (); segment hides'.

Current Phase 3 registry.rs compile_plugin requires `const ID`, so a 0-byte file raises PluginError::Compile { message: 'missing required const ID' } rather than silently hiding.

Two valid paths: update the spec to match impl ('0-byte file is a compile error'), or update the impl to match spec (treat empty source as silent skip). Decide which, then add a test asserting the chosen behavior.

**Acceptance:** spec and impl agree on 0-byte behavior; a registry test pins the chosen path.

title: PluginError design follow-ups (non_exhaustive review, source chain, path sharing)
description:
Deferred items from Phase 2 type-design review of `crates/linesmith/src/plugins/errors.rs`. None blocking for Phase 2-6 of lsm-ewa; revisit when concrete callers surface.

**Items:**

1. **Re-evaluate `#[non_exhaustive]` on PluginError.** Phase 2 kept the attribute as a defensive default. The type-design reviewer argued it's overkill for a currently-crate-private concept and forces needless `_ =>` arms in doctor matchers. Audit once lsm-l35 (doctor) wires a match site: if every variant needs explicit handling, drop the attribute; if we truly expect variants to grow across releases, keep it. Decision should be recorded in this bead's notes.

2. **Wire `std::error::Error::source()` chain for `Compile`.** Today the variant carries `message: String` (rhai's error stringified). When Phase 3 wires `rhai::Engine::compile_file()`, preserve the underlying `rhai::ParseError` as `source` so doctor / debug output can surface line+column info programmatically instead of regex-scraping the formatted message.

3. **Consider `Arc<Path>` in `Compile` + `IdCollision`.** Current `PathBuf` is fine at today's scale (< 100 plugins). If a long-running daemon retains error history across many reloads, the clone-cost becomes a real thing. Revisit when daemon mode lands (or after profiling shows a hotspot).

4. **`Timeout` → `WallclockTimeout` rename.** Would disambiguate from `ResourceExceeded { limit: MaxOperations }`. Kept the current name in Phase 2 to avoid bikeshed; if the wrapper work (Phase 5) makes the ambiguity more real, rename then.

**Acceptance:** at least #1 decided + recorded; #2 wired when real rhai::ParseError hits the code (Phase 3). #3 + #4 re-triaged.

title: Add serde::Serialize to DataDep for telemetry + explain output
description:
DataDep currently has Debug + Display (lowercase tokens matching the `@data_deps` header syntax). When telemetry, a `linesmith explain` command, or debug-dump CLI lands, it'll want to emit a segment's declared deps as structured data (JSON / TOML). Add `#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]` at that point.

**Scope:**
- Add serde feature flag (if not already on by default for this crate).
- Derive Serialize + Deserialize on DataDep with the lowercase-token representation (`#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`).
- Keep Display impl identical — both should produce the same wire name.

**Why deferred:** no current consumer. Adding now risks adding a serde dep for no immediate use. Pair with whichever feature first needs structured output.

**Acceptance:** `serde_json::to_string(&DataDep::Git)` returns `"git"`; round-trip deserialization succeeds.

title: Add data_deps declaration-vs-usage truthfulness test harness
description:
Phase 1 of lsm-ewa landed `Segment::data_deps()` but nothing enforces that a segment's declared deps match the sources its `render()` actually reads. A segment can call `ctx.usage()` without declaring `DataDep::Usage` and the code compiles + runs (lazy accessor initializes on demand). Once the runtime's union-and-prefetch pass lands with real fetchers, under-declaring segments will trigger lazy fetches that the prefetch skipped — silently slower, defeating the whole point of declaring deps.

**Scope:**
- Instrument `DataContext` with a test-only accessor-tracker (e.g., `#[cfg(test)]` fields that record which lazy accessors were called).
- Add a contract test per built-in segment: build the segment, run `render` against an instrumented DataContext, assert the touched accessor set is a SUBSET of `data_deps()`.
- Run the same harness against plugin/rhai segments in Phase 2 testing.

**Why now vs later:** the bug doesn't manifest until real fetchers land (lsm-y6m for usage, lsm-8jl for git). File as a follow-up so the invariant gets a typed enforcement before it can rot.

**Acceptance:** a built-in segment that reads `ctx.usage()` without declaring `DataDep::Usage` fails the contract test with a clear message.

title: Wire cargo-audit into mise + add audit task
description:
Pre-release runbook (docs/ops/release-runbook.md) and spec §Release runbook both want `cargo audit` as a pre-flight check for new advisories against Cargo.lock. Currently `cargo audit` is neither installed nor a mise task, so the runbook can't literally reference it.

**Scope:**
- Add `cargo-audit` as a mise-managed tool in .mise.toml [tools]
- Add a `mise run audit` task (maps to `cargo audit --quiet --deny warnings` or similar)
- Update the pre-flight section of docs/ops/release-runbook.md to include the new task
- Optionally include it in `mise run check` so CI catches advisories on every PR too

**Acceptance:** fresh clone + `mise install` gets cargo-audit; `mise run audit` exits 0 on clean state; runbook references it as a real task, not a note.

title: ADR-0012: Per-process execution model (daemon deferred to v0.2+)
description:
Codify the per-process decision from data-fetching-strategy.md §10 + session discussion into a MADR v4.0 ADR.

Decision: each invocation spawns a fresh linesmith process; no persistent daemon. Daemon mode documented as v0.2+ escape hatch if cold-start measurements exceed targets despite optimizations.

Acceptance:
- docs/adrs/0012-per-process-execution.md exists, follows 0000-template.md
- Status: accepted
- Cites data-fetching-strategy.md §10
- Captures: per-process rationale (simplicity, no IPC, matches all competitors), daemon-mode tradeoffs, measurement criteria for revisiting
- Independent of ADR-0009/0010/0011 (can be written in parallel with them)
notes: Fourth of 4 ADRs. Independent. Shorter than the others (~80 lines).
close_reason: ADR-0012 written: docs/adrs/0012-per-process-execution.md. Locks in per-process invocation model for v0.1. Daemon mode documented as the v0.2+ escape hatch if cold-start target can't be hit with per-process + segment-driven lazy loading (ADR-0010). All 4 competitor Claude Code statuslines surveyed use per-process — no daemon precedent. Data-fetching architecture from ADR-0010 composes cleanly with future daemon mode (DataContext ports to daemon-owned without segment-code changes).

title: Research: CCometixLine (Rust peer) data sources + Rust patterns
description:
ccstatusline-widget-internals.md nailed the TS dominant tool. CCometixLine (~2.7k⭐, Rust/TOML) is our closest architectural peer. Cross-check to confirm (a) no different rate-limit data source (i.e., they also hit /api/oauth/usage or use a different path), (b) Rust-specific patterns worth adopting: binary size, HTTP client, caching, credential reading, gix usage.

Acceptance:
- Locate the repo, identify maintainer + license
- Document data-source cascade (HTTP endpoint? cache? JSONL fallback?)
- Note any rate-limit source that ccstatusline doesn't use
- Catalog Rust-specific implementation choices (ureq vs reqwest, cache format, credential reader)
- Compare binary size / startup time claims if documented
- If nothing new: close with verdict 'parity with ccstatusline findings; no new patterns to adopt'
notes: Lower priority than the earlier batch since ccstatusline internals are already documented. Main value is Rust-peer comparison.
close_reason: CCometixLine hits identical /api/oauth/usage endpoint with same oauth-2025-04-20 beta header — no new data source. Rust patterns captured in docs/research/ccometixline-rust-patterns.md: adopt ureq + serde + chrono, config-driven base_url/TTL/timeout (CCometixLine), lock file + 429 handling (ccstatusline), cargo release profile tuning (lto/strip/codegen-units=1/panic=abort). Avoid: npm-subprocess User-Agent. Recommend skipping claude-powerline/claudia-statusline/felipeelias — design space is covered.

title: Research: rate-limit data source per plan tier (free / pro-max / api)
description:
Tier-aware rate-limit fallback: refine derivation heuristic if users report mismatches.

ADR-0011 (docs/adrs/0011-rate-limit-data-source.md) locks in the primary derivation:
- `stripe_subscription` + `hasOpusPlanDefault=true` → Max
- `stripe_subscription` + `hasOpusPlanDefault=false` → Pro
- missing/other → Free

Inferred from Max-tier capture only (maintainer on Max plan, not downgrading). Pro and Free rows are educated guesses.

Acceptance (repurposed — no longer a proactive spike):
- Stay open as a catch-all for tier-mismatch bug reports
- If a user files 'my tier shows as X but I'm on Y' — update the table in ADR-0011 via a follow-up ADR (per immutability rule)
- If a volunteer with Pro/Free access offers to capture the endpoint response + oauthAccount block, their data updates the table via the same follow-up ADR
- Close when either the table is confirmed correct across all three tiers OR v0.2 ships without tier-mismatch reports
notes: Repurposed from proactive spike to passive issue-tracker. The original 'capture free-tier response' acceptance is unblocked only by community contribution; not on linesmith v0.1 critical path. Reason: maintainer is on Max plan and not downgrading.
close_reason: Tier detection is out of scope for v0.1 per ADR-0011. No surveyed Claude Code statusline (ccstatusline, CCometixLine, claudia-statusline, claude-powerline) does tier detection; they all display raw endpoint utilization %. linesmith follows the same approach. Tier-aware behavior deferred to v0.2+ and gated on a concrete product need. If we ever want it, derivation can pull from ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.billingType + hasOpusPlanDefault, but that's a future ADR.

title: Research: distinguish bare repo / linked worktree / main checkout
description:
Stdin `workspace.git_worktree {name, path}` tells us WHICH worktree, not which KIND. For correctness-first worktree isolation (ccstatusline#190) we need to know:

- Main checkout: `.git` is a directory
- Linked worktree (`git worktree add`): `.git` is a file with `gitdir: ...` pointer
- Bare repo: no worktree; repo discovery returns kind=bare

`gix` exposes this via `Repository::kind()`. Need to confirm API, test against fixtures.

Acceptance:
- Document gix API for repo/worktree kind detection
- Confirm behavior on all three layouts + submodule edge case
- File follow-up bead for worktree-kind signal in workspace segment (or dedicated segment) if useful

title: Research: detect effort/thinking level from JSONL or settings
description:
Effort segment with reliable detection. ccstatusline-style JSONL parse for `<local-command-stdout>Set model to ... with {EFFORT} effort` has reliability holes documented in docs/research/claude-data-files.md §7:
1. /model invocations that DON'T change effort emit 'Kept model as X' (no effort) — regex misses
2. /effort-only invocations emit a different marker — regex misses
3. Cancelled runs write nothing to JSONL
4. Session-start with no transcript writes returns undefined

Implement with dual-source approach:
- JSONL backwards scan for BOTH /model and /effort markers (two regexes)
- Configured fallback default (xhigh per docs)
- Optional: monitor additionalModelOptionsCache in ~/.claude.json once Anthropic populates it

Forward-compat: store unknown effort tokens as {value, known: false}. Known set: low | medium | high | xhigh | max.
notes: Reopened after docs/research/claude-data-files.md §7 documented reliability holes the prior close reason didn't capture. Original close pointed only to ccstatusline's single-regex approach.

title: Add rustfmt.toml + clippy.toml + taplo.toml for consistent tooling
description:
Relies on tool defaults today, which drift across Rust versions and contributors. Mirrors jbabin91/autocomplete-rs configs as the baseline.

**Scope:**
- rustfmt.toml: pin max_width, imports_granularity, group_imports, reorder_imports, use_field_init_shorthand, other stable rustfmt options. Start from autocomplete-rs config verbatim and tweak if 'cargo fmt' produces unexpected changes on existing code.
- clippy.toml: pin msrv (to match Cargo.toml rust-version = 1.80), cognitive-complexity-threshold, disallowed-types/methods, doc-valid-idents if needed.
- taplo.toml: TOML formatter config — column_width, align_entries, reorder_keys. Consistent formatting for Cargo.toml, *.toml configs, fixtures/*.toml.

**Process:**
1. Copy the three files from autocomplete-rs as starting points
2. Run 'cargo fmt', 'cargo clippy -- -D warnings', 'taplo format --check' — fix any drift
3. Add 'taplo format --check' or similar to mise check task if not there already

**Acceptance:** mise run check is still green; diffs from 'cargo fmt --all -- --check' are stable; future contributors get the same formatting regardless of their rustfmt/clippy/taplo version (within reason).

title: PR template + bug/feature issue templates + ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml
description:
Add GitHub Issue + PR templates. **GitHub Issues are the intake funnel for beads** — external users file issues, maintainers triage them into bd. Templates must collect bead-ready information so conversion is friction-free.

**Scope:**
- .github/pull_request_template.md: Summary + Resolves (bead footer reminder, lsm-xxx format) + Test plan checkbox (mise run check, mise run test, manual smoke if UI/output changed)
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml: fields shaped to become a bead description directly:
  - Steps to reproduce
  - Expected vs actual
  - linesmith --version
  - OS + terminal + shell
  - Claude Code version
  - Relevant env vars (NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, COLUMNS, TERM, COLORTERM)
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml: fields matching a feature-bead shape:
  - Problem statement (what's missing, who is it hurting)
  - Proposed solution
  - Alternatives considered
  - Links to related ADR / spec / idea / existing bead
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml: contact_links pointing to oakoss GitHub Discussions for questions. Do NOT disable blank issues — some reports genuinely don't fit a template and forcing a template creates friction.

**Workflow documented in CONTRIBUTING.md (lsm-00f):**
- External reporters file a GH Issue via template
- Maintainer triages into a bead (bd create) if real work; closes issue with 'Tracked as lsm-xxx' pointer
- Or: keeps issue open, links bead in description, closes issue when bead closes

**Skip for now:** CODEOWNERS (single maintainer), separate security template (oakoss/.github/SECURITY.md covers it).

**Acceptance:** new PRs open with the template prefilled; bug and feature templates appear on 'New Issue' with fields that a maintainer can copy/paste directly into a bead description.

title: Write project-specific CONTRIBUTING.md for linesmith
description:
Overrides the org-level oakoss/.github CONTRIBUTING.md for this repo. linesmith's workflow differs meaningfully — beads is the source of truth for tracking work, and GitHub Issues serve as the public intake funnel.

**Scope (~100 lines max):**
- Quick start: mise install, mise run check, mise run test
- How work gets done:
  - External users: file a GitHub Issue (bug or feature template); maintainer triages into a bead (bd) and links back
  - Internal contributors: bd ready to find/claim work; read AGENTS.md for the full contract; docs/specs/ for feature-area specs
- Docs pipeline summary: research → ideas → ADRs → specs → beads (point at docs/README.md for details)
- Pull requests: conventional commits enforced by cog (pre-commit hook), wait for review before committing, no proactive commits, one logical change per commit, bead footer in subject (lsm-xxx)
- Optional callout on the review cadence: de-slopify → multi-agent PR review → Codex review → close bead → commit is the project's standard slice cycle
- Org-wide guidelines pointer: link to oakoss/.github for code of conduct, security reporting, support channels

**Why project-specific:**
- AGENTS.md is heavy; CONTRIBUTING.md is a softer on-ramp that points at it
- Beads + GitHub-Issues-as-intake workflow is unusual and worth explaining
- mise + lefthook + cog stack differs from Bun/pnpm projects the org-level CONTRIBUTING assumes
- Docs pipeline is distinctive

**Keep inherited from org-level:**
- CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
- SECURITY.md
- SUPPORT.md
- FUNDING.yml

**Acceptance:** a new external user reads CONTRIBUTING.md and knows in under 2 minutes how to file an issue and what happens next; a new internal contributor knows how to find work, how PRs get reviewed, and where the pipeline docs live.

title: Extend workspace segment to surface worktree name in hybrid format
description:

**Depends on:** lsm-5wu (spec decides exact format).

title: README install section + docs/ops/release-runbook.md
description:
Part of lsm-c2i epic. User-facing install docs + contributor-facing release runbook + Rust-specific dev setup.

**Context:** oakoss/.github provides org-wide CONTRIBUTING.md which says 'check the project's README for package manager, installation steps, development commands, test instructions.' linesmith's README must satisfy that pointer.
